evidence_summary: Company disclosed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions, debtor-in-possession operation and accelerated obligations; filing warns that security recovery is uncertain but does not establish old-common cancellation.
adjudication_note: Verified bankruptcy; keep below S until a plan or court order proves cancellation or no recovery for old common equity.

evidence_summary: Company disclosed Chapter 11 and a plan under which creditors receive reorganized equity while existing common and preferred interests receive no distribution and are canceled for no consideration.
adjudication_note: Primary filing directly supports common-equity death; this is the clean S boundary the radar should learn.

evidence_summary: Delisting followed a completed merger; each old common share converted into the right to receive 0.85 OceanFirst common share plus cash for fractional shares.
adjudication_note: Sharadar delisting action is real, but it is not a severe negative event or common-equity death.

evidence_summary: Delisting followed a completed cash merger. Common and Class B common shares converted into the right to receive $19.00 per share; other listed classes also received stated cash consideration.
adjudication_note: The delisting is a paid merger completion, not a severe negative event.

evidence_summary: The SPAC announced redemption and dissolution. Public shares were canceled only after becoming rights to receive the redemption amount; warrants and rights expired without a liquidating distribution.
adjudication_note: The common-share outcome is redemption consideration, so the bankruptcy label is false even though warrants expire worthless.

evidence_summary: After a distribution and merger, each Clean Earth common share converted into the right to receive $15.00 cash; aggregate transaction consideration was disclosed as approximately $3.04 billion.
adjudication_note: The exchange exit is transaction mechanics with cash consideration, not equity death.

evidence_summary: The completed merger converted each American Woodmark common share into 5.150 MasterBrand common shares plus cash for fractional shares.
adjudication_note: Shareholders received stock consideration; delisting is not a negative-death label.

evidence_summary: The completed merger canceled each outstanding common share only after converting it into the right to receive $19.00 cash without interest.
adjudication_note: Cancellation wording must not override the explicit per-share cash merger consideration.

evidence_summary: Nasdaq's Hearings Panel determined to delist the securities for missed audited-financial-statement and Form 20-F deadlines; trading was to be suspended June 2 while appeal and relisting remained possible.
adjudication_note: The delisting determination and suspension are official and material, but appeal and relisting paths make the event reversible and below A++.

evidence_summary: SVB Financial Group confirmed its March 17 Chapter 11 filing, which triggered defaults or repayment obligations across multiple debt instruments; the cited filing did not establish old-common cancellation.
adjudication_note: Relabel the price-only discovery as a confirmed Chapter 11 cause; keep below S until common-equity treatment is proven.

evidence_summary: Nasdaq determined to delist the parent's ADSs after its Hartshorne Mining subsidiary filed Chapter 11; suspension was effective March 5 and OTC quotation remained possible.
adjudication_note: Primary evidence explains the price dislocation, but the bankruptcy scope is a subsidiary and parent securities could continue OTC, so the event is not A++ or S.

evidence_summary: The confirmed plan became effective March 5, 2026; all equity interests outstanding before the effective date, including common stock, were canceled for no consideration, while new common equity was issued to noteholders.
adjudication_note: A 180-day follow-up filing resolves the provisional plan language and proves final old-common cancellation with no consideration.

evidence_summary: The SPAC public shares were canceled only after becoming the right to receive the stated redemption amount.
adjudication_note: Redemption consideration makes this a corporate-action control, not bankruptcy or equity death.

evidence_summary: The company and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the Southern District of Texas.
adjudication_note: Primary evidence confirms Chapter 11; retain below S until final old-common recovery or cancellation is proven.

evidence_summary: The company and certain subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the Southern District of Texas.
adjudication_note: Primary evidence confirms Chapter 11; retain below S until final old-common recovery or cancellation is proven.

evidence_summary: The company filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition in Delaware and continued operating as debtor-in-possession.
adjudication_note: Primary evidence confirms Chapter 11; retain below S until final old-common recovery or cancellation is proven.

evidence_summary: The company disclosed Chapter 11 and expected that common holders would receive no distributions and that common equity would be canceled under a plan, but the cited filing described an expected future result rather than an effective plan.
adjudication_note: The expected zero recovery is highly material but remains below S until a confirmation order or effective-date filing proves final old-common treatment.

evidence_summary: The SPAC public shares were canceled only after becoming the right to receive a stated redemption amount.
adjudication_note: Redemption consideration makes this a corporate-action control rather than bankruptcy or common-equity death.

evidence_summary: The company and direct and indirect subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 7 petitions; the filing describes liquidation and warns common holders could experience a significant or complete loss.
adjudication_note: Company-wide Chapter 7 is a legal liquidation rather than a rescue-oriented reorganization; it establishes the legal-death boundary even though final distribution amounts were not yet quantified.

evidence_summary: The confirmed plan became effective and canceled old common stock, but old common holders received approximately 5% of the new common equity, with possible additional contingent shares.
adjudication_note: Cancellation language alone must not produce S: explicit new-equity recovery for old holders keeps this as a severe but non-zero-recovery boundary.

evidence_summary: The company and debtor subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions, triggering defaults and subsequent exchange delisting, without final old-common treatment in the cited evidence.
adjudication_note: Primary evidence confirms Chapter 11 and material legal consequences; retain below S until old-common recovery or cancellation is final.

evidence_summary: On the plan effective date, all previously issued and outstanding ModivCare equity interests were canceled, released and extinguished for no consideration; new plan securities went to creditors and other entitled parties.
adjudication_note: The effective plan and explicit no-consideration cancellation prove final old-equity death.

evidence_summary: After asset sales, the company assigned all remaining assets for creditors, ceased business operations, filed an effective certificate of dissolution, closed its stock-transfer books and stated that no liquidating distribution was expected and stockholders would suffer a complete loss.
adjudication_note: Operational cessation, formal dissolution, creditor assignment and explicit complete stockholder loss jointly prove truth, legal and common-equity death.

evidence_summary: Each Thermon common share converted, subject to election and proration, into CECO shares plus $10 cash, $63.89 cash, or CECO shares; the transaction also paid approximately $329.4 million aggregate cash consideration.
adjudication_note: The exchange exit followed a completed cash-and-stock merger with explicit consideration, not equity death.

evidence_summary: Each Calavo common share converted into 0.9790 Mission Produce shares plus $14.85 cash, with cash for fractional shares; aggregate consideration included about 17.5 million Mission Produce shares and $265.9 million cash.
adjudication_note: Explicit stock and cash consideration makes the delisting a merger-mechanics control.

evidence_summary: Each outstanding Mister Car Wash common share was canceled only after converting into the right to receive $7.00 cash, while dissenting shares retained statutory appraisal rights.
adjudication_note: Cancellation wording is transaction mechanics because common holders received explicit cash consideration or appraisal rights.

evidence_summary: The selected filing discussed a January 2021 default and a Chapter 11 plan of Adara Enterprises that became effective June 15, 2021; it did not establish a new same-entity hard event near the November 9 price and volume crash.
adjudication_note: Retain the observed market dislocation only as P evidence; the stale subsidiary bankruptcy passage cannot supply R, L or E or upgrade severity.

evidence_summary: The selected filing discussed a January 2021 default and a Chapter 11 plan of Adara Enterprises that became effective June 15, 2021; it did not establish a new same-entity hard event near the November 4 price crash.
adjudication_note: Retain the observed market dislocation only as P evidence; the stale subsidiary bankruptcy passage cannot supply R, L or E or upgrade severity.

evidence_summary: Nasdaq had identified unpaid listing fees as a possible delisting basis, but the company paid the fees in full on November 26 and Nasdaq notified it on November 27 that the matter was closed; the same-day official evidence therefore contradicts an unresolved delisting cause for the price crash.
adjudication_note: Keep the observed price dislocation as P evidence only. A resolved listing-fee matter cannot supply negative R, L or E and should be a temporal/refutation control.

evidence_summary: The company exchanged 320 million warrants for 240 million newly issued ordinary shares at $0.60 per share; after closing it reported 269,325,176 ordinary shares outstanding, making the exchange shares approximately 89% of post-transaction shares three days before the heavy-volume collapse.
adjudication_note: The contemporaneous primary filing supplies a concrete extreme-dilution cause. It is severe but capital-structure-repairable and therefore remains A rather than A++ or S.

evidence_summary: The business combination completed and the former CGC Class A security was reclassified into successor PubCo Series A common stock, which was approved for Nasdaq listing under the new symbol FAC; the detected CGCTU exchange exit is a SPAC security transition, not a negative company delisting.
adjudication_note: Reject the severe-negative label: successor common stock and warrants remained Nasdaq-listed after the business combination.

evidence_summary: Upon closing the business combination, GigCapital7 units ceased trading while Hadron Energy common stock and public warrants began Nasdaq trading as HDRN and HDRNW; redeeming public holders also received the stated trust-account redemption price.
adjudication_note: The unit termination is transaction mechanics with continued successor listings, not company distress or common-equity death.

evidence_summary: PureTech voluntarily ended its Nasdaq ADS listing because most trading, liquidity, price discovery, investors and governance were centered in the United Kingdom; ordinary shares remained listed on the London Stock Exchange and the company cited the cost and administrative burden of a dual listing.
adjudication_note: This is a real but ordinary listing-access reduction with a continuing primary LSE venue, not a forced delisting or severe equity-loss event.

evidence_summary: WM Technology voluntarily delisted after citing Nasdaq constraints on cannabis-market strategy, limited investor liquidity and analyst coverage, and ongoing disclosure and regulatory costs; it expected continued quotation through OTC Markets.
adjudication_note: The venue and liquidity loss are genuine, but the event is board-elected, retains an expected OTC path and does not establish severe operating or equity death.

evidence_summary: Lavoro voluntarily exited Nasdaq amid a challenging Brazilian market, low trading volume, a limited public shareholder base and public-company costs; the company said these conditions reduced liquidity and U.S. capital-market access, with no assurance that an OTC market would exist.
adjudication_note: The official filing supports a material loss of market access and liquidity under operating stress, but the board-elected action remains solvable and below A++ or S.

evidence_summary: Telefónica voluntarily ended its NYSE ADS listing to reduce administrative burden and cost under its simplification plan; ordinary shares remained on the Spanish exchanges, ADS holders could exchange into those shares, and a Level 1 ADR program was intended to facilitate U.S. OTC trading.
adjudication_note: This is a real U.S. venue exit but continuing Spanish liquidity and ADR alternatives make it an ordinary listing-consolidation event rather than severe company damage.

evidence_summary: Old Market Capital cited low trading volume, public-company cost and regulatory burdens, expected annual savings, and a desire to redirect resources; it anticipated OTCID quotation but gave no assurance that an OTC market or trading would continue.
adjudication_note: The filing supports a material and uncertain contraction in public-market access under weak liquidity, while the voluntary and potentially reversible nature keeps it below A++.

evidence_summary: Tile Shop executed a 1-for-3,000 reverse split followed by a matching forward split as a going-dark transaction: holders below 3,000 shares received $6.60 cash per share, continuing holders retained the same share count, and the company proceeded toward Nasdaq delisting and SEC deregistration to save more than $2.4 million annually.
adjudication_note: Cash-out protection for small holders and unchanged ownership counts for continuing holders prevent an equity-death label; the remaining public-liquidity loss is an ordinary B event.

evidence_summary: Glen Burnie said likely future Nasdaq non-compliance would inevitably result in delisting, while analyst coverage and active trading were absent and reporting costs were significant; it sought OTCQX quotation but stated there was no guarantee that a broker or trading market would continue.
adjudication_note: The action was formally voluntary but preempted expected listing failure and carried uncertain replacement liquidity, making it materially negative but still solvable and below A++.

evidence_summary: Carver voluntarily moved from Nasdaq to expected OTCQX quotation to reduce recurring expense and gain strategic flexibility; it planned to keep annual audited statements and quarterly information available while its regulated bank continued OCC call reporting.
adjudication_note: The Nasdaq exit reduces venue quality and reporting obligations but preserves an expected OTCQX path and ongoing financial disclosure, so it remains B.

evidence_summary: Taitron's board concluded that Nasdaq listing, SEC compliance and management-resource costs outweighed the benefits; with fewer than 300 holders it planned deregistration, and said Pink-market quotation depended on market makers with no assurance that trading would continue.
adjudication_note: The public-market downgrade and reporting loss are real, but no weak operating event, forced listing failure or direct equity impairment was established, so the event remains B.

evidence_summary: GENFIT voluntarily removed its Nasdaq ADSs to simplify its corporate structure and improve operating efficiency while stating that Euronext Paris remained its primary regulated market and that its financial foundation was strong.
adjudication_note: A continuing primary Euronext listing and explicit operational-simplification rationale make this an ordinary venue-consolidation event, not severe company or equity damage.

evidence_summary: Light & Wonder consolidated its Nasdaq and ASX dual listing into a sole primary ASX listing to align capital-market presence with its shareholder base and growth plans; holders could convert shares into equivalent ASX-traded CDIs, continue holding for OTC trading, or sell before suspension.
adjudication_note: The deep and liquid ASX replacement market and equivalent CDI conversion preserve centralized liquidity, keeping the Nasdaq exit at B.

evidence_summary: Associated Capital voluntarily left NYSE and suspended SEC reporting to reduce legal, audit, listing and management costs; it applied for OTCQX quotation and intended continued shareholder information, while acknowledging that continued market making was not guaranteed.
adjudication_note: This is a cost-driven venue downgrade with an intended OTCQX and information path, not evidence of weak operations, forced delisting or common-equity death.

evidence_summary: Sunrise's Nasdaq ADS listing was designed as a roughly nine-month transitional venue after its Liberty Global spin-off; it delisted to streamline reporting and save costs while its Class A shares continued on the SIX Swiss Exchange and ADSs could trade OTC before program termination.
adjudication_note: The planned short-lived U.S. listing and continuing SIX market show listing consolidation rather than a severe negative corporate event.

evidence_summary: Brooge Energy's board cited the lack of an active market for its securities and the continuing expense, regulatory burden and management attention required by Nasdaq and Exchange Act reporting; the announcement did not identify a continuing home exchange or assured replacement trading venue.
adjudication_note: The filing establishes a material contraction in public-market access rather than mere listing consolidation, but the voluntary and potentially reversible action remains below A++.

evidence_summary: Contemporaneous filings describe a Nasdaq qualification halt and appeal concerning publicly held shares, bid price and stockholders' equity; the company issued shares to cure one deficiency and Nasdaq announced resumed trading. No court insolvency, bankruptcy petition, liquidation or old-common treatment was disclosed in the event window.
adjudication_note: Reject the Sharadar bankruptcy/liquidation label; the documented event is a listing-compliance dispute and trading halt.

evidence_summary: Nasdaq ordered suspension because the security closed at $0.10 or less for ten consecutive business days after a prior reverse split and while under panel monitoring; the company sought a hearing and expected OTC trading. No insolvency filing or liquidation was identified.
adjudication_note: Reject the bankruptcy/liquidation metadata label and retain the official low-price suspension only as a separate listing-event candidate.

evidence_summary: Nasdaq issued a delisting determination under the Low Priced Stocks Rule after ten consecutive days at or below $0.10 while the company was under a mandatory panel monitor; trading was to be suspended despite appeal. The filing contains no bankruptcy or liquidation proceeding.
adjudication_note: The official cause is listing-rule failure, so the Sharadar bankruptcy/liquidation classification is rejected.

evidence_summary: Nasdaq denied continued listing because Carbon Revolution failed the minimum shareholders' equity rule, had not filed its Form 20-F and could not demonstrate timely completion of a strategic transaction; trading was suspended and the company did not appeal. Going-concern uncertainty was disclosed, but no formal insolvency or liquidation was filed.
adjudication_note: Severe financial and listing stress do not by themselves establish bankruptcy; reject the legal-event label until a court or company insolvency filing exists.

evidence_summary: Inspire's common stock moved to OTCQB, management described the change as supporting operating focus, and the company said it would continue SEC periodic and current reporting. Nearby filings show debt-for-equity exchanges and going-concern risk but no bankruptcy petition, court insolvency or liquidation.
adjudication_note: Debt cancellation language and liquidated-damages clauses are financing terms, not old-common cancellation or liquidation; reject the bankruptcy metadata label.

evidence_summary: ECD Automotive described Nasdaq minimum-bid-price and market-value-of-listed-securities deficiencies, reverse splits and an equity line intended to restore listing compliance. The event-window filings contain no bankruptcy petition, court insolvency or liquidation.
adjudication_note: Reject the bankruptcy/liquidation metadata label; the documented event is listing remediation and a reverse split.

evidence_summary: Harrison Global received a Nasdaq determination after failing to regain the minimum bid price within the second 180-day compliance period. Nearby filings cover a reverse split, repurchase authorization and PIPE financing, not insolvency.
adjudication_note: Reject bankruptcy/liquidation and retain the contemporaneous low-price listing failure as a separate event.

evidence_summary: Dynamix is a SPAC whose filing describes redemption and eventual liquidation only as the contractual consequence if it fails to complete a business combination by its deadline. The conditional going-concern language does not establish a filed bankruptcy or current liquidation on the detector date.
adjudication_note: Reject the bankruptcy/liquidation label; a future SPAC deadline and cash redemption condition are not a present insolvency filing.

evidence_summary: Bowen Acquisition disclosed Nasdaq delisting for failing to maintain 400 total shareholders, followed by a hearing decision and trading suspension. No bankruptcy petition, court insolvency or liquidation was disclosed.
adjudication_note: Reject the bankruptcy/liquidation metadata label and retain the shareholder-count listing event only.

evidence_summary: Ambipar Emergency Response disclosed that its parent and an affiliate sought judicial recovery in Brazil and that the company filed a concurrent U.S. Bankruptcy Code action in the Southern District of Texas; subsequent court relief protected group operations and assets while the Brazilian proceeding was considered.
adjudication_note: The contemporaneous company filing establishes court-supervised cross-border insolvency, but it does not establish cancellation or zero recovery for old ordinary shares.

evidence_summary: FlexShopper disclosed continuing events of default, acceleration of approximately $164.5 million principal plus interest and fees, termination of its subsidiary's servicing role and an end to further advances. These facts establish severe debt default, not a bankruptcy filing on October 24; the later Chapter 11 petition was filed on December 22, 59 days after the detector date.
adjudication_note: Reject the dated bankruptcy label and reclassify the contemporaneous evidence as debt default/acceleration. Later bankruptcy evidence must not retroactively validate an earlier event date.

evidence_summary: SemiLux received a Nasdaq staff determination after failing to cure the minimum bid price deficiency, lacking the $5 million stockholders' equity needed for a second compliance period and failing to file its 2025 Form 20-F. Suspension was scheduled while the company sought a hearing and extended stay.
adjudication_note: The forced delisting has multiple contemporaneous operating, capital and reporting causes. It is material but remains below A++ because the company sought appeal and the filing does not establish insolvency or old-common destruction.

evidence_summary: Bitcoin Depot and its subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 to conduct an orderly wind-down and asset sale. Nasdaq stated that the bankruptcy directly caused suspension and delisting under Rules 5101, 5110(b) and IM-5101-1; the company did not intend to appeal and warned of significant or complete investor loss.
adjudication_note: This queue contains no separate Bitcoin Depot bankruptcy detector thread, so the bankruptcy-caused delisting carries the primary severe-event evidence. Keep below S until a confirmed plan or court order resolves old-common recovery.

evidence_summary: Society Pass disclosed that Nasdaq determined to delist its common stock because the company and a subsidiary had commenced Chapter 11 cases. This is a verified listing consequence of the already-adjudicated same-company, same-date bankruptcy event, not a second independent severe event.
adjudication_note: Link to CAND-14606774787152120897 in the same stable-security and event-date chain. Preserve the true delisting fact but exclude it from independent hard-label counts and training duplication.

evidence_summary: Granite REIT voluntarily left NYSE because of persistently low U.S. trading volume, operating costs, administrative efficiency and structure simplification. Its units continued on the Toronto Stock Exchange and qualified for OTCQX trading from January 2, 2026.
adjudication_note: The loss of NYSE access is real, but continuing TSX primary trading and OTCQX access make this a listing consolidation rather than a severe negative corporate event.

evidence_summary: HCyte completed a 1-for-1,000 reverse split, leaving about 255,246 common shares outstanding while 494,579,117 preferred shares became convertible into about 494,579 post-split common shares. The same filing disclosed $272,500 of notes convertible at a 35% discount to the lowest recent trading price.
adjudication_note: The split itself is proportional, but the contemporaneous discounted notes and preferred conversion overhang make the event materially different from an ordinary compliance-only reverse split.

evidence_summary: Ascent Solar completed a 1-for-5,000 reverse split that reduced old common shares from about 23.74 billion to 4.81 million. Immediately afterward, convertible notes became 18.4 million post-split shares and preferred stock became another 7.4 million shares; 30.61 million shares were outstanding and one holder controlled 52.1%.
adjudication_note: Post-split conversions created roughly 25.8 million shares against only about 4.81 million split-adjusted old common shares and transferred majority voting control. This is a dilution/control event, not a mechanical split label.

evidence_summary: PharmaCyte completed a 1-for-1,500 reverse split, proportionately reducing about 2.4 billion outstanding shares to about 1.6 million and reducing authorized common shares from 50 billion to 33,333,334. The company described the action as preparation for a national-exchange uplisting and future financing or strategic transactions.
adjudication_note: No contemporaneous issuance, holder-percentage change or destructive equity treatment was established. Keep the true action as a B boundary rather than a hard short label.

evidence_summary: ValueSetters completed a 1-for-2,000 reverse split and changed its name to Netcapital immediately before a merger. About 416,590 split-adjusted shares remained before 1,666,360 merger shares were issued, producing about 2,082,950 total shares and the NCPL ticker transition.
adjudication_note: The split is a verified transaction mechanic within a merger and ticker transition. It should not be learned as an independent negative or dilution signal.

evidence_summary: Greenlane selected and completed a 1-for-750 reverse split so its shares could trade on a split-adjusted basis from June 27. Nasdaq had required the company to effect a split and achieve a $1 minimum closing bid as a condition of continued listing.
adjudication_note: This is a high-ratio distress signal and listing-remediation action, but the reviewed evidence does not itself establish new-share dilution or old-equity destruction.

evidence_summary: Femto Technologies announced a 1-for-500 reverse split that reduced approximately 279.95 million subordinate voting shares to about 559,895. The action applied uniformly, preserved relative ownership and was undertaken to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance.
adjudication_note: The filing expressly says relative interests were unchanged. Preserve the compliance signal while keeping this below material-dilution grade.

evidence_summary: Esports Entertainment completed a 1-for-400 reverse split, reducing about 426 million shares to 1.065 million and authorized shares from 500 million to 1.25 million. It acted to address Nasdaq low-price and minimum-bid rules and stated that future shareholder approval would be sought to restore capital-raising capacity.
adjudication_note: The split preserved holder percentages and proportionately reduced authorized capital. Future financing intent is material context but is not an executed issuance on the event date.

evidence_summary: Aclarion completed a 1-for-335 reverse split, reducing about 169.4 million common shares to about 500,000 while leaving 200 million authorized. The same filing reported an underwritten unit offering with about $14.55 million gross proceeds; the next filing priced another 506,803 common shares for about $4.7 million.
adjudication_note: The authorized-share headroom expanded dramatically and the next-day registered direct common issuance alone roughly matched the entire post-split common count. Treat as material dilution review rather than an ordinary split.

evidence_summary: Sharps Technology completed a 1-for-300 reverse split to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance. Both outstanding and authorized common shares were reduced proportionately, with authorized shares falling from 500 million to 1,666,667.
adjudication_note: The filing states that authorized and outstanding shares were reduced proportionately and no adverse holder effect was intended. Keep as a compliance boundary, not a hard dilution label.

evidence_summary: Hyperscale Data sought and then effected a 1-for-300 reverse split. The capital structure included preferred shares sold for $10 million whose conversion at 85% of market price became available only after reverse-split approval, plus rights to purchase additional discounted convertible notes.
adjudication_note: Although the May 16 split filing shows a proportional reduction of outstanding shares, approval activated discounted preferred conversion and associated convertible-note financing, creating material dilution exposure.

evidence_summary: Avalo completed a 1-for-240 reverse split, reducing approximately 192.39 million common shares to about 801,611 while leaving authorized common shares unchanged. Holder percentages and voting power remained substantially unchanged; Nasdaq later confirmed bid-price compliance under a one-year panel monitor.
adjudication_note: The unchanged authorized ceiling greatly expands issuance capacity relative to outstanding shares, but no contemporaneous issuance was established. Keep the action as a B compliance and capital-structure boundary.

evidence_summary: Jet.AI completed a 1-for-225 reverse split to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance. The action applied uniformly, proportionately adjusted derivative securities, left authorized common shares unchanged and did not materially alter holder ownership percentages.
adjudication_note: This first reviewed split is a proportional listing-remediation boundary. Its failure to produce durable compliance becomes material context for the later April 2026 repeat event, but should not be back-propagated into this event's grade.

evidence_summary: XTI Aerospace completed a 1-for-250 reverse split as a condition to a best-efforts public offering of 1,454,546 post-split common shares for about $20 million, plus 72,727 placement-agent warrant shares. Before the offering it reported about 1,848,121 post-split shares outstanding.
adjudication_note: The newly offered shares equal roughly 79% of the pre-offering post-split common count, and the split was expressly required for closing. This is a material financing/dilution event rather than an ordinary compliance split.

evidence_summary: Aditxt completed a 1-for-250 reverse split that left approximately 1,031,102 common shares outstanding. The split was primarily intended to cure Nasdaq minimum-bid noncompliance, left authorized shares unchanged and proportionately adjusted options, units and warrants.
adjudication_note: The issuer was under listing pressure and retained expanded issuance capacity, but the reviewed event filing establishes no same-date issuance or conversion. Keep at B pending a separately dated financing event.

evidence_summary: Polyrizon implemented a 1-for-250 reverse split, reducing approximately 1.332 billion shares to about 5.328 million while authorized capital remained unchanged. Nasdaq simultaneously issued a delisting determination because securities issued under a March purchase agreement, particularly Series A warrants with alternate cashless exercise, had caused substantial shareholder dilution and raised public-interest concerns.
adjudication_note: The primary source explicitly links the financing structure to substantial dilution and a Nasdaq public-interest delisting concern. The reverse split is part of that material capital-structure chain, not a standalone mechanical action.

evidence_summary: Healthcare Triangle completed a 1-for-249 reverse split while leaving two billion authorized common shares unchanged. On the filing's split-adjusted basis, outstanding shares rose from about 22,759 at December 2024 to 5,831,829 at June 2025; the equity roll-forward includes about 4.262 million shares from cashless warrants and 1.388 million acquisition shares.
adjudication_note: The roughly 256-fold increase in split-adjusted outstanding shares before the split is dominated by warrant and acquisition issuance. This is a verified extreme-dilution context, while the split itself remains proportionate.

evidence_summary: Oriental Culture completed a 1-for-220 consolidation, reducing approximately 381.52 million ordinary shares to about 1.738 million. Issued, outstanding, authorized and unissued shares were consolidated together; the purpose was Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance, and a special cash dividend was scheduled on the post-consolidation basis.
adjudication_note: Authorized capital was consolidated proportionately and the concurrent action included a shareholder cash distribution. This is a true compliance event but not a dilution or severe-equity-loss label.

evidence_summary: Garden Stage completed a 200-for-1 consolidation of authorized, issued and outstanding Class A shares to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance. Nasdaq confirmed compliance on March 20 and closed the matter.
adjudication_note: The consolidation was proportional and successfully cured the cited deficiency. It is useful as a negative control against treating every high-ratio split as material dilution.

evidence_summary: Linkers Industries completed a 1-for-250 reverse split of Class A and Class B shares to maintain Nasdaq listing. Issued and unissued shares and par value were adjusted proportionately, about 1.357 million Class A and 250,000 Class B shares remained, and shareholder percentage interests were not altered except for fractional rounding.
adjudication_note: The source establishes a proportional dual-class consolidation with no separate issuance. Keep as a B listing-remediation boundary.

evidence_summary: Jet.AI completed a 1-for-200 reverse split, reducing approximately 129.36 million shares to about 646,812 while leaving authorized shares unchanged. This followed its 1-for-225 compliance split only about seventeen months earlier; the company again cited Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance and later confirmed the deficiency was cured.
adjudication_note: The second high-ratio split in seventeen months proves the prior remediation was not durable and compounds authorized-share headroom. Repeated failed remediation is materially stronger than a first proportional compliance split, but remains below A++ because no court, delisting or old-equity outcome occurred.

evidence_summary: Erayak paired a 1-for-220 reverse split with an at-the-market sales agreement for up to $10 million. The prospectus also records July registered-direct issuance of 12,396,000 shares and immediately exercisable pre-funded warrants for 18,216,246 shares; pre-split shares outstanding reached about 187.9 million.
adjudication_note: The ATM capacity was close to the issuer's pre-split market capitalization at the cited $0.061 price, and it followed large pre-funded-warrant issuance. Treat the split and financing as one dilution chain rather than an ordinary compliance action.

evidence_summary: Cheetah Net completed a 1-for-200 reverse split after a 1-for-16 split in October 2024. Its split-adjusted filing records a January 2026 private placement of 167,250 shares for approximately $40.14 million and shows 391,177,712 pre-current-split Class A shares reduced to 1,955,889.
adjudication_note: This is a repeat remediation accompanied by a material private placement and a sharp intervening increase in the share base. The linked capital change warrants A, while no court or old-common extinguishment supports A++.

evidence_summary: Vivakor's second reviewed reverse split, 1-for-200 after a 1-for-30 split in 2022, reduced about 410.07 million shares to 2.05 million while leaving 500 million authorized. A Nasdaq Hearings Panel conditioned continued listing on bid-price compliance and issued a Public Reprimand Letter for financings above the 19.99% threshold without prior shareholder approval.
adjudication_note: The repeat split, unchanged authorized ceiling and contemporaneous Nasdaq finding of financing-rule violations form a material dilution and governance chain. It remains below A++ because listing continued conditionally and old common was not canceled.

evidence_summary: Mingteng implemented a 1-for-200 split after establishing a $100 million ATM facility. Class A shares outstanding rose from 19,766,054 on December 8, 2025 to 242,334,931 on January 21, 2026 before being reduced to about 1,211,675 by the split; authorized and issued classes were consolidated proportionately.
adjudication_note: The roughly twelvefold share-count increase over six weeks is the decisive signal, not the mechanical split ratio. The contemporaneous ATM facility and issuance establish extreme dilution exposure despite proportional consolidation.

evidence_summary: Bit Brother completed a 1-for-1,000 split after 1-for-15 and 1-for-10 prior splits. Immediately beforehand it offered 184,615,385 Class A shares plus Class D and Class E warrants for up to 369,230,770 additional shares at $0.065, while Nasdaq had already issued a low-price delisting determination.
adjudication_note: Repeated reverse splits, a share-and-double-warrant package and active listing pressure make this a strong A dilution sample. It stays below A++ because the event-date evidence does not establish court supervision or old-common cancellation.

evidence_summary: Midwest Holding effected a 1-for-500 reverse split and Delaware reincorporation while resetting authorized capital to 24 million shares. The action supported a proposed Nasdaq uplisting and public offering after earlier institutional private financing, with cash paid for fractional shares.
adjudication_note: The split was a capitalization and uplisting mechanic rather than evidence of distress or an immediate dilutive conversion. Keep as a B boundary even though separate financing transactions existed.

evidence_summary: Mobiquity completed a 1-for-400 reverse split effective for FINRA trading on September 9, 2020 and reduced authorized common shares to 100 million. FINRA applied the temporary MOBQD symbol for twenty business days; no contemporaneous issuance or conversion was established.
adjudication_note: The contemporaneous 8-K/A resolves the apparent date conflict with a later 10-Q that stated September 29: FINRA's trading effective date was September 9. This remains a proportional B corporate-action boundary.

evidence_summary: Sharadar's 1-for-250 IGLDF action is corroborated by the FINRA-linked OTC daily-list record and independent market-history datasets. It followed the issuer's 1-for-100 split in August 2019; the company was then a shell after disposing of its principal asset.
adjudication_note: The repeated extreme consolidation in a shell company is materially stronger than a first mechanical split. Because no contemporaneous SEC filing or financing amount was available, cap the event at A and keep source-strength review visible before downstream import.

evidence_summary: The English High Court sanctioned Argo Blockchain's restructuring plan. The company delisted from the London Stock Exchange, issued 2,885,767,520 new ordinary shares for bondholder debt exchange and 25,250,465,800 shares to Growler for loan conversion, assets and exit capital, and changed the ADS ratio from 10:1 to 2,160:1.
adjudication_note: This is not an ordinary reverse split: it is a court-approved rescue recapitalization with massive debt-to-equity issuance, LSE delisting and an ADS ratio reset. Existing equity was not shown as canceled, so A++ is appropriate rather than S.

evidence_summary: Next Technology completed a 1-for-200 reverse split after a registered direct offering of 25,313,256 shares and pre-funded warrants for 34,686,744 shares at about $0.15. The warrants were immediately exercised and all underlying shares issued; authorized shares remained unchanged after the split.
adjudication_note: The $9 million financing issued 60 million shares immediately before the split and followed an earlier 2023 high-ratio split. This is a verified dilution chain, not a standalone compliance split.

evidence_summary: Lowe's reported a $9.27 billion shareholders' deficit, but also $1.628 billion quarterly net earnings and $3.35 billion operating cash flow. The deficit improved from $9.917 billion at fiscal year-end and reflects its leveraged capital-return structure rather than an acute loss of operating viability.
adjudication_note: Negative book equity is factual but not independently a hard short event. Strong profitability and cash generation make this a B accounting boundary; debt and capital returns must be assessed separately.

evidence_summary: Box reported a $338.361 million stockholders' deficit while earning $17.726 million in the quarter. It repurchased $114.4 million of stock during the quarter and authorized a further $500 million expansion, leaving about $445 million available under the repurchase plan.
adjudication_note: The deficit is materially affected by discretionary capital return while the issuer remains profitable. Keep as a B false-hard-event boundary and do not infer insolvency from the equity line alone.

evidence_summary: Bath & Body Works reported a $1.133 billion shareholders' deficit including $822 million of treasury stock. First-quarter net income was $183 million and operating cash flow was $244 million; the deficit improved from $1.451 billion a year earlier.
adjudication_note: Treasury stock and accumulated capital returns explain much of the deficit while earnings and operating cash remain positive. This is a B accounting boundary, not evidence of equity death.

evidence_summary: Dell reported a $1.404 billion stockholders' deficit, consisting in part of $16.149 billion of treasury stock against $6.343 billion of retained earnings. Quarterly net income was $3.438 billion, operating cash flow was $4.081 billion, and cash plus available revolver capacity totaled $17.462 billion.
adjudication_note: The negative equity is dominated by cumulative repurchases, not current operating distress. High earnings, cash flow and liquidity make this a strong B control against a naive negative-equity short signal.

evidence_summary: Rent the Runway reported a $53.3 million stockholders' deficit, an $18.9 million quarterly net loss, $3.8 million operating cash burn, $37.1 million cash and $157.1 million long-term debt. A troubled debt restructuring exchanged $234.2 million of debt for 26,175,193 shares, and a new ATM permits up to $40 million of sales.
adjudication_note: Unlike profitable buyback-driven deficits, this case combines recurring losses, cash consumption, debt-for-equity dilution, PIK flexibility and additional funding needs. Management states twelve-month liquidity is sufficient, which keeps it below A++.

evidence_item: Nasdaq suspension after OFAC action
evidence_summary: Pingtan disclosed that Nasdaq suspended trading on December 9, 2022 in response to OFAC actions that placed the company, its chief executive and related vessels on the Specially Designated Nationals list.
adjudication_note: The official issuer filing establishes a direct regulatory cause and trading suspension before the detected price episode. This is a hard event, but not proof that common equity was legally canceled, so it remains below S.

evidence_summary: Sequential Brands disclosed bankruptcy-court first-day motions, debtor-in-possession financing, sale procedures and a liquidating plan; later filings recorded sales of its remaining brands during the detected price-crash episode.
adjudication_note: The detector is a late market consequence of an already active Chapter 11 liquidation chain. Keep the event at A++ rather than S because the reviewed passage does not itself prove cancellation or zero distribution for old common equity.

evidence_item: effective resale registration
evidence_summary: Femto disclosed effectiveness of a resale registration covering up to 233,352,911 common shares, including 2,011,616 shares behind pre-funded warrants, up to 27,960,512 behind Series A warrants and up to 201,315,663 behind Series B warrants.
adjudication_note: The same-day filing gives a concrete extreme dilution overhang and aligns with the detected market episode. It is a material A sample, not A++, because there is no court process, forced suspension or old-common extinguishment.

evidence_item: Part III narrative
evidence_summary: Eloxx reported only $0.2 million of cash at June 30, 2024, lacked the financial resources to prepare its quarterly statements and expected substantial doubt about going concern because cash resources were insufficient for twelve months of planned operations.
adjudication_note: The warning preceded the first detector in a 30-day clustered price episode and supplies a primary non-price cause. Financial distress is severe, but no bankruptcy, receivership or equity cancellation supports A++.

evidence_item: receivership
evidence_summary: New York regulators closed Signature Bank and appointed the FDIC receiver. The FDIC transferred deposits and substantially all assets to a bridge bank and stated that shareholders and certain unsecured debt holders would not be protected.
adjudication_note: The official resolution action clearly precedes and explains the later market-volume episode. Shareholders were not protected, but the source does not conclusively establish final zero recovery or legal cancellation of every common share, so cap at A++.

evidence_summary: The 90-day SEC cause search found no contemporaneous issuer filing or official action that explains the isolated volume detector for Wave Sync Corp.
adjudication_note: Do not train a negative event label from volume behavior alone. Retain only as a discovery false-positive control unless new dated primary evidence appears.

evidence_item: going-concern assessment
evidence_summary: Nano Magic discussed historical operating losses and negative cash flow but also cited increased revenue, positive working capital and a recent capital raise, concluding that capital resources were sufficient to maintain operations for the next twelve months.
adjudication_note: The nearby primary filing contains an explicit mitigating liquidity conclusion rather than a new hard event. Reject the price-only detector as a negative label while retaining it as a boundary case.

evidence_item: going concern; subsequent offering
evidence_summary: Envoy Medical had $3.739 million cash at year-end and recurring losses that caused its auditor to express substantial doubt about going concern. A February 2026 offering provided about $27.73 million net through 47,946,150 common shares and 27,053,850 pre-funded warrants, accompanied by 120,000,000 additional Series A warrants; management expected the proceeds to fund at least twelve months.
adjudication_note: Reject the unstable gross-margin detector as the causal description but retain the same-date primary event after reclassification. The financing mitigates immediate cash failure while imposing extreme dilution, supporting A rather than A++ or S.

evidence_item: going concern; annual liquidity
evidence_summary: Sky Quarry reported $35,370 of cash at December 31, 2025, a $12.198 million annual net loss, $3.273 million of operating cash use, recurring operating losses and a net capital deficiency that caused substantial doubt about going concern. Nasdaq had also determined to delist the common stock for continued minimum-bid noncompliance.
adjudication_note: Reject the unstable gross-margin ratio as the event description and reclassify to evidenced liquidity and operating distress. Funding or restructuring may still change the outcome, and no bankruptcy or old-common cancellation supports A++ or S.

evidence_item: merger agreement
evidence_summary: The generic SF1 revenue ratio was mathematically incomparable, and the contemporaneous filing showed a merger in which each Two Harbors common share would convert into the right to receive $10.80 in cash.
adjudication_note: Reject the negative revenue-collapse label. The transaction changes comparability and provides explicit positive consideration to common holders.

evidence_item: bank operating metrics
evidence_summary: The detector produced revenue_yoy=-6.248 while requiring current revenue greater than zero, which implies a negative or incomparable prior denominator. Eastern Bank instead reported interest yields, deposit costs and noninterest income, for which generic industrial revenue is not the correct stress metric.
adjudication_note: A value below -100% cannot represent ordinary positive-to-positive revenue decline under the detector formula. Use net interest income, credit quality and regulatory capital for banks.

evidence_item: metric review context
evidence_summary: The detector produced revenue_yoy=-17.084 while requiring positive current revenue. This necessarily reflects a negative or incomparable prior-period denominator rather than a valid 1,708% revenue decline.
adjudication_note: Reject the event-type label at the mathematical boundary. Any genuine biotechnology funding or clinical event must be detected and evidenced separately.

evidence_item: bank restructuring context
evidence_summary: The detector produced revenue_yoy=-10.010 with positive current revenue, proving a negative or incomparable prior denominator. Patriot's presentation described a bank restructuring platform with robust capital and liquidity goals, not a valid generic revenue-collapse measurement.
adjudication_note: Reject the generic revenue label and evaluate the bank with net interest margin, credit losses, regulatory capital and deposit funding metrics.

evidence_item: transaction accounting context
evidence_summary: The detector produced revenue_yoy=-4.644 despite requiring positive current revenue, so the prior denominator is negative or incomparable. The nearby filing concerned transaction accounting and a change in ownership of seller subsidiaries, further breaking simple revenue comparability.
adjudication_note: Reject the metric-derived negative label. A mine sale or ownership transition must be evaluated as a separate corporate transaction with asset and consideration evidence.

evidence_item: SPAC going concern
evidence_summary: Agriculture & Natural Solutions Acquisition Corp is a blank-check shell. Its going-concern paragraph concerns the deadline and uncertainty of completing an initial business combination, not an operating company's cash coverage of short-term debt.
adjudication_note: Restricted trust assets, sponsor working capital and the contractual combination deadline must be separated. Reject the generic cash-to-short-debt event label.

evidence_item: SPAC going concern
evidence_summary: Harvard Ave Acquisition Corp is a blank-check shell whose going-concern language arises from financing and acquisition-plan costs and the need to complete a business combination, rather than an operating liquidity collapse.
adjudication_note: Reject the generic cash-ratio label. Any liquidation, redemption or failed-combination event must be detected separately with trust-account and common-holder consideration evidence.

evidence_item: trust account
evidence_summary: Idea Acquisition Corp disclosed that $350 million of IPO and private-placement proceeds was placed in its trust account. The SF1 cash-to-current-debt value of zero excludes or misclassifies restricted SPAC trust assets and is not an operating distress measure.
adjudication_note: Reject the cash-short-debt label. SPAC review must use trust assets, redemption liability, working capital outside trust and the combination deadline.

evidence_item: going concern and liquidity
evidence_summary: Nauticus Robotics had $7.017 million cash, used $23.004 million in operations and had a working-capital deficit with insufficient cash for twelve months. It raised $34.717 million from ATM common stock and Series B preferred financing, yet management and the auditor still disclosed substantial doubt about going concern.
adjudication_note: Reject the unstable gross-margin ratio as the causal label and reclassify to primary-evidenced liquidity distress. Investor support and further equity issuance may fund operations, so the outcome remains below A++ and S.

evidence_item: going concern and liquidity
evidence_summary: Humacyte had $50.5 million cash, only $1.4 million product revenue, a $726.8 million accumulated deficit and a senior secured term-loan facility of up to $77.5 million. It stated that liquidity would be insufficient beyond one year without timely commercial cash flow or additional capital and concluded that substantial doubt existed about going concern.
adjudication_note: Reject the unstable gross-margin delta and retain a reclassified financing-dependent distress event. Commercial sales and new capital can still alter the outcome, preventing A++ or S.

evidence_item: liquidity and early-stage operations
evidence_summary: Atomera is an early-stage licensing company with limited revenue, making a -1,145.5 percentage-point gross-margin delta denominator-sensitive. It reported about $41.1 million of cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments, $39.9 million working capital and $4.6 million quarterly operating cash use without a going-concern warning.
adjudication_note: Reject gross-margin collapse as a major negative label. Intermittent licensing revenue makes the ratio unstable, while available liquidity is material relative to the reported quarterly burn.

evidence_item: regulated utility equity financing
evidence_summary: The York Water Company is a regulated water utility and announced a public common-stock offering. A generic cash-to-current-debt threshold does not distinguish utility working-capital structure, rate-regulated funding or committed capital access.
adjudication_note: Reject the generic cash-short-debt label. Utilities require sector-specific debt maturity, interest coverage, rate-case and capital-program measures rather than a cross-sector cash ratio.

evidence_item: LTM cash flow and adjusted EBITDA
evidence_summary: Duluth reported trailing-twelve-month free cash flow of $16.6 million versus negative $25.2 million in the prior period and positive adjusted EBITDA. Its subsequent 10-Q described a new $100 million revolver at a lower rate through April 2030; customary default language was not an actual default.
adjudication_note: Reject the single-quarter coverage signal. Retain only if LTM coverage, covenant breach, missed payment, going concern or a comparable primary distress fact is present.

evidence_item: quarterly cash-flow comparability
evidence_summary: The detector compared a first-quarter free-cash-flow value with the immediately preceding fourth quarter for an apparel company. The reviewed filing did not establish a contemporaneous going-concern, payment-default or covenant-breach event, so the quarter-over-quarter turn is seasonality-sensitive.
adjudication_note: Reject quarter-over-quarter free-cash-flow turn-negative. Recalculate on same-quarter year-over-year and LTM bases before any distress classification.

evidence_item: merger and tender-offer context
evidence_summary: Destination XL's reviewed disclosure concerned an all-cash tender offer while the company was already subject to a merger agreement. The detector compared first-quarter free cash flow with the immediately preceding holiday quarter and did not identify a primary distress event.
adjudication_note: Reject the quarter-over-quarter free-cash-flow label. Transaction context and retail seasonality break the assumed comparability; require same-quarter YoY or LTM deterioration plus primary distress evidence.

evidence_item: quarterly operating cash-flow statement
evidence_summary: Sportsman's Warehouse is a seasonal retailer, while the detector compared first-quarter free cash flow with the immediately preceding fourth quarter. The reviewed filing showed the quarterly cash-flow statement but did not establish default, covenant breach or going-concern distress.
adjudication_note: Reject the previous-quarter FCF turn-negative signal and suppress the sibling single-quarter coverage candidate in the same review thread. Require same-quarter YoY or LTM confirmation.

evidence_item: quarterly cash-flow comparability
evidence_summary: Signet is a strongly seasonal jewelry retailer, and the detector compared first-quarter free cash flow with the immediately preceding holiday quarter. The reviewed filing did not identify a contemporaneous going-concern, covenant-breach or payment-default event.
adjudication_note: Reject quarter-over-quarter free-cash-flow turn-negative. Use same-quarter year-over-year and LTM cash-flow measures for seasonal retailers.

evidence_item: cash and debt position
evidence_summary: Shoe Carnival reported $129 million of cash and marketable securities, no debt, $7 million of share repurchases and reaffirmed fiscal-year guidance. A negative single-quarter EBIT-to-interest-expense ratio cannot indicate debt distress when the company reports no debt.
adjudication_note: Reject the coverage label. Require actual funded debt, meaningful cash interest and a distress fact before applying an interest-coverage crisis rule.

evidence_item: liquidity and balance sheet
evidence_summary: Uranium Energy reported $488.1 million of cash and cash equivalents, $581.6 million of current assets, $17.8 million of current liabilities and $563.8 million of working capital. Interest expense was immaterial relative to liquidity, so the negative single-quarter coverage ratio reflects operating-stage losses rather than debt distress.
adjudication_note: Reject the interest-coverage label. Mining-development operating losses require separate cash-runway and financing-dilution review; they are not evidence of a payment or covenant crisis.

evidence_item: cash and debt position
evidence_summary: Hurco reported more than $50 million in cash and cash equivalents, no debt, a 300-basis-point gross-margin expansion and a 40% narrowing of net loss per share. Customary default clauses in a credit agreement are not an actual default.
adjudication_note: Reject the single-quarter interest-coverage label because the company reported no debt and improving operating metrics.

evidence_item: capital resources and liquidity
evidence_summary: Antero Resources generated $859.1 million of operating cash flow in the quarter, had $1.6 billion of available borrowing capacity and stated that operating cash flow plus available credit would cover normal operations, debt service, capital spending and contingencies for at least twelve months.
adjudication_note: Reject the cash-short-debt label. For producing E&P companies, use operating cash flow, hedge-adjusted leverage, debt maturities and committed liquidity instead of spot cash divided by current debt.

evidence_summary: After previously ceasing operations and terminating all employees, Ontrak's board approved a voluntary Chapter 7 petition and every director resigned effective immediately.
adjudication_note: Chapter 7 plus ceased operations is a severe terminal-company event, but the filing does not explicitly prove the recovery or cancellation outcome for old common equity; keep below S until that terminal equity evidence is obtained.

evidence_summary: Soleno's exchange exit followed a completed Neurocrine tender offer and merger in which each common share was entitled to $53.00 cash.
adjudication_note: The delisting is transaction mechanics after paid merger consideration, not a severe negative event or common-equity death.

evidence_summary: Marine Products' completed merger converted each common share into 0.232 MasterCraft shares plus $2.43 cash before NYSE delisting.
adjudication_note: Shareholders received stock and cash consideration; the exchange exit is not a negative-death label.

evidence_summary: Enhabit common shares were cancelled only after being converted into the right to receive $13.80 cash in the completed merger.
adjudication_note: Cancellation wording must not override explicit per-share cash merger consideration.

evidence_summary: Tri Pointe Homes' completed merger converted each eligible common share into the right to receive $47.00 cash.
adjudication_note: The delisting followed cash consideration and is not a severe negative event.

evidence_summary: CSG Systems common shares were converted into the right to receive $80.70 cash in a completed merger before Nasdaq delisting.
adjudication_note: Paid merger consideration makes this a corporate-action control, not a negative-death label.

evidence_summary: NuCana disclosed 151.9 million ordinary shares before a financing sequence that included 61.3 million issued shares, 209.8 million fully exercised pre-funded warrants and a subsequent 9.12 billion ordinary shares issued through warrant exercises, for about GBP 8.0 million net proceeds.
adjudication_note: The A++ assessment belongs to the realized financing chain, not to the later one-for-200 ADS ratio change by itself; exclude this reverse-split proxy from hard-label training until the primary financing event is represented separately.

evidence_summary: Sun Country's completed merger converted each common share into $4.10 cash plus 0.1557 Allegiant common shares before Nasdaq delisting.
adjudication_note: The exchange exit is completed-merger mechanics with explicit stock and cash consideration, not a negative-death event.

evidence_summary: Udemy's completed merger converted each common share into 0.800 Coursera common shares, with cash only for fractional shares, before Nasdaq delisting.
adjudication_note: Common holders received listed acquirer shares; option cancellation language must not be mistaken for common-equity death.

evidence_summary: Marin Software's Chapter 11 plan proposed paying allowed claims in full, distributing an estimated $2.5-$4.0 million residual to holders of old interests, and then retiring and cancelling those interests.
adjudication_note: The old ownership instrument is terminal, but explicit residual cash recovery prevents a zero-recovery S label and disproves the detector's Chapter 7 liquidation implication.

evidence_summary: WeightWatchers' Chapter 11 plan cancelled old equity but voluntarily allocated its holders 9% of reorganized common equity on a pro-rata basis, subject to stated dilution and milestone conditions.
adjudication_note: Cancellation of the old security is severe, but the explicit 9% reorganized-equity recovery keeps this below S and shows why Chapter 7 boilerplate must not be treated as an actual liquidation.

evidence_summary: Azul initiated a court-supervised Chapter 11 reorganization while continuing ordinary airline operations, with a stated objective of eliminating more than $2.0 billion of funded debt and reducing lease obligations.
adjudication_note: The filing proves severe legal and balance-sheet restructuring, but continued operations and no explicit old-common outcome keep the event below S and refute the liquidation implication.

evidence_summary: iCoreConnect and a wholly owned subsidiary filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions after Nasdaq trading had already been suspended.
adjudication_note: Chapter 11 is verified and severe, but the filing does not establish liquidation, old-common cancellation or zero recovery, so S is not supported.

evidence_summary: After Silicon Valley Bank was closed and placed into FDIC receivership, SVB Financial Group filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition on March 17, 2023.
adjudication_note: The hard event is the receivership and parent bankruptcy chain, not the later five-day price move used to discover it; keep this price proxy excluded from hard-label training and below S without explicit old-common outcome.

evidence_summary: Future Mobility Solutions moved to OTC trading after a delisting determination and stated that its financial condition was stable and operations would continue.
adjudication_note: The source proves a listing event, not bankruptcy or liquidation; retain it as a detector-mismatch control.

evidence_summary: China Liberal Education's Nasdaq suspension resulted from a delinquent Form 20-F and an unsuccessful stay request, not an insolvency filing.
adjudication_note: The detector's bankruptcy classification is false; the filing supports only a listing-compliance suspension.

evidence_summary: Zapp's Nasdaq delisting followed failures to regain the $1 minimum bid price and $35 million minimum market value requirements.
adjudication_note: This is a genuine adverse listing event but not bankruptcy or liquidation; reject the detected family and retain the mismatch as a control.

evidence_summary: Vincerx received an immediate Nasdaq delisting determination after prolonged sub-$1 trading and ineligibility for a cure period because of a prior reverse split.
adjudication_note: The detector's bankruptcy/liquidation family is unsupported; the filing proves a listing-compliance failure only.

evidence_summary: Cutera disclosed that its Nasdaq delisting followed commencement of voluntary Chapter 11 proceedings; the nearby Chapter 7 wording was only a contingent DIP default clause.
adjudication_note: Chapter 11 and delisting are verified and severe, but neither an actual Chapter 7 conversion nor old-common zero recovery is proven; do not promote to S.

evidence_summary: Benson Hill and its wholly owned subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions after disclosing insufficient liquidity for the company's long-term strategy.
adjudication_note: The legal and liquidity distress is verified, but the filing does not establish liquidation or terminal old-common treatment, so S is unsupported.

evidence_summary: Omega Therapeutics filed a voluntary Chapter 11 petition and separately disclosed related listing consequences.
adjudication_note: The filing proves Chapter 11, not Chapter 7 liquidation or zero recovery for old common; retain the A++ ceiling.

evidence_summary: WinVest's securities were suspended because the SPAC failed to complete a business combination by the Nasdaq panel deadline.
adjudication_note: The source supports a SPAC listing failure, not bankruptcy or liquidation.

evidence_summary: Aquaron disclosed a Nasdaq panel delisting determination and its remaining review window, with no bankruptcy filing in the cited evidence.
adjudication_note: The detector's bankruptcy family is unsupported; preserve the row as a listing-event mismatch control.

evidence_summary: Crown Electrokinetics received a Nasdaq delisting determination and planned to request reconsideration; the evidence contains no insolvency proceeding.
adjudication_note: The detected bankruptcy/liquidation label is false; only a contested listing event is supported.

evidence_summary: Intelsat's filing described customary DIP credit agreement defaults and a contingent Chapter 7 conversion clause within Chapter 11 proceedings that had begun in May 2020; it did not disclose a new liquidation event near the September 29 price move.
adjudication_note: The price detector found a move, but the available primary source is stale bankruptcy context and contractual boilerplate rather than a temporally aligned new cause.

evidence_summary: Dreamland disclosed that it had regained Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance and that the listing matter was closed shortly before the detected volume crash.
adjudication_note: The closest primary evidence is mitigating rather than adverse, so the market move cannot be promoted to a hard event label.

evidence_summary: Planet Labs described customary note covenants and default provisions and explicitly stated that no such events had occurred as of April 30, 2026.
adjudication_note: A calculated interest-coverage screen is not itself a distress event, and the filing expressly negates an actual default.

evidence_summary: Snowflake's quarterly filing recited ordinary indenture covenants and hypothetical default consequences but disclosed no actual payment default, covenant breach, insolvency or acceleration.
adjudication_note: Contractual default boilerplate does not verify a distress event; retain this as a negative control for the ratio detector.

evidence_summary: Scorpius disclosed an NYSE American trading suspension and delisting proceeding based on listing suitability; the source did not disclose a bankruptcy or liquidation filing.
adjudication_note: The nearby note contained only customary default clauses; the actual event was a listing action, so the bankruptcy detector family is unsupported.

evidence_summary: IMAC Holdings disclosed promissory notes whose customary default provisions included hypothetical bankruptcy and insolvency events; it did not disclose that any such event had occurred.
adjudication_note: The detector matched contractual language, not an insolvency proceeding; preserve the row as a source-semantics control.

evidence_summary: Globavend confirmed that all Series B warrants from a $15 million public offering closed on June 27 were exercised around a one-for-200 reverse split effective July 21.
adjudication_note: The hard signal is the completed financing and realized warrant exercise linked to the extreme reverse split, not the split ratio alone.

evidence_summary: SUNation stated that its reverse split was primarily intended to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance; the nearby shelf filing contained only generic future issuance language.
adjudication_note: No contemporaneous executed financing or non-proportional common-equity harm was established, so this remains a B boundary rather than an A dilution event.

evidence_summary: Lichen disclosed recent issuance and sale of 20 million shares at $0.14 and 15 million shares at $0.18, including exercised pre-funded warrants, shortly before its March reverse split.
adjudication_note: The recent executed low-price issuance makes this materially different from a compliance-only proportional reverse split.

evidence_summary: Algorhythm reported 476,359,875 shares outstanding, including shares issued through Series B warrant exercises from its December financing, immediately before a one-for-200 reverse split.
adjudication_note: The score-derived A++ priority reflects scale, but the reviewed event remains A because the evidence proves recapitalization and dilution rather than terminal equity loss.

evidence_summary: Scorpius priced a $12.5 million underwritten offering of 12.5 million common shares or pre-funded warrants at $1.00 shortly after its one-for-200 reverse split.
adjudication_note: The follow-up offering supplies the causal financing context; manual A records severe dilution risk without treating a non-terminal recapitalization as A++.

evidence_summary: SINTX stated that its reverse split was primarily intended to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance and later announced that compliance had been restored.
adjudication_note: The later prospectus passage described generic sale methods and did not prove an executed financing tied to the split.

evidence_summary: Ascent Solar's split reduced about 92 million outstanding shares to 500,000 while leaving 500 million authorized shares unchanged and leaving outstanding convertible notes and preferred stock unaffected.
adjudication_note: The unchanged authorized capacity and unaffected convertibles create concrete post-split dilution headroom beyond a proportional compliance action.

evidence_summary: EZGO exchanged existing warrants for 1,246,000 ordinary shares and 10,879,534 pre-funded warrants shortly before a 150-for-one reverse split and a disclosed $100 million ATM facility.
adjudication_note: Executed warrant exchange plus immediate additional issuance capacity establishes a financing chain; manual A avoids overstating it as terminal.

evidence_summary: 22nd Century implemented a reverse split without proportionately reducing authorized shares after registering up to 28.35 million shares underlying pre-funded warrants and 65.26 million underlying other warrants.
adjudication_note: The warrant overhang and unchanged authorization make this a material dilution setup, while the absence of terminal equity treatment keeps the manual grade at A.

evidence_summary: A Nasdaq Hearings Panel determined to delist Reviva for failure to meet the minimum-bid requirement after the compliance period, with the common stock moving to OTCQB.
adjudication_note: This is a completed forced national-exchange exit after exhausted compliance process, materially impairing liquidity and financing access even though OTC trading continues.

evidence_summary: BIO-key disclosed Nasdaq suspension and a forthcoming Form 25 after it failed to regain minimum-bid compliance; a subsequent filing added delinquent periodic reporting as another delisting basis.
adjudication_note: The suspension and Form 25 process are concrete listing-loss consequences; multiple unresolved compliance failures support A without implying bankruptcy or equity cancellation.

evidence_summary: China SXT offered 12 million Class A ordinary shares and pre-funded warrants for up to 54,666,666 additional shares shortly before the detected one-for-150 reverse split.
adjudication_note: The executed offering capacity is the material signal; manual A recognizes severe dilution without treating the reverse split as terminal equity loss.

evidence_summary: Cyngn announced that all outstanding Series B cashless warrants had been fully exercised six days before the detected reverse split, following a public offering of common shares and pre-funded warrants.
adjudication_note: Realized warrant exercise supplies primary financing context and distinguishes the event from a compliance-only split.

evidence_summary: American Lithium voluntarily left Nasdaq while retaining listings on the TSX Venture Exchange and Frankfurt Stock Exchange and seeking an immediate OTCQX quotation after a minimum-bid deficiency.
adjudication_note: The U.S. venue loss matters but does not imply security death because active home-market listings and planned OTCQX continuity remain.

evidence_summary: WiSA entered a registered direct offering for 225,834 post-split common shares at $3.321 per share plus concurrent private-placement warrants two days after its one-for-150 reverse split.
adjudication_note: The near-immediate executed financing is direct causal context for the post-split capital structure.

evidence_summary: Nxu stated that its one-for-150 reverse split was primarily intended to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance, and the adjustments applied proportionately to outstanding securities.
adjudication_note: A later generic shelf-registration passage does not prove an executed financing tied to the split.

evidence_summary: Haoxi offered 9 million Class A ordinary shares and disclosed up to 176,034,979 additional shares underlying 16,999,998 pre-funded warrants immediately before the detected reverse split.
adjudication_note: The disclosed share overhang makes this a high-priority dilution event, but absent terminal old-common treatment the reviewed grade remains A.

evidence_summary: Generations Bancorp voluntarily withdrew from Nasdaq and deregistered while arranging continuous OTCQX quotation under the same ticker.
adjudication_note: National-exchange liquidity and reporting access contract, but the security continues on OTCQX and no insolvency or cancellation is shown.

evidence_summary: GIBO implemented a share consolidation as part of its Nasdaq minimum-bid remediation plan and subsequently disclosed that it had regained compliance while remaining under panel monitoring.
adjudication_note: The filing supports listing remediation and later compliance, not a separately executed dilutive financing.

evidence_summary: BYND Cannasoft disclosed a one-for-190 reverse split whose stated purpose was to regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance, with its common shares continuing to trade under the same listing.
adjudication_note: This is a listing-remediation corporate action; no contemporaneous executed dilution evidence was established.

evidence_summary: Greenwave implemented a one-for-150 reverse split to increase its per-share price and regain Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance, proportionately converting outstanding shares.
adjudication_note: The selected primary evidence supports only a proportional compliance action, not realized dilution.

evidence_summary: ToughBuilt implemented a one-for-150 reverse split for Nasdaq bid-price compliance and subsequently received confirmation that it had regained compliance.
adjudication_note: Although authorized shares were not reduced, the reviewed window does not establish an executed financing or convertibles sufficient to promote this above B.

evidence_summary: The selected SEC source belongs to Verb Technology and reports its Nasdaq bid-price compliance; it does not substantiate the queue's TONX security identity or the detected corporate action.
adjudication_note: A filing for a different issuer cannot verify the detected event; retain this row to test point-in-time identifier joins.

evidence_summary: Sophiris disclosed a six-month principal-payment deferral with interest current and only a hypothetical acceleration upon future default; its actual Nasdaq delisting had occurred more than two months before the detected price move.
adjudication_note: The nearby evidence is either mitigating debt relief or stale listing history, so it does not establish a new cause for the May 19 market move.

evidence_summary: Youngevity disclosed that its lender had issued notice of actual defaults under its loan and security agreement before the later detected one-day price crash.
adjudication_note: The filing verifies a real debt event, but the later price detector is only a discovery proxy and must remain excluded from hard-label training until the primary default date is represented directly.
