adjudication_note: A++ ceiling: the petition and listing loss are realized, but expected or possible loss is not final proof that old common was canceled without recovery.

evidence_item: sole operating subsidiary voluntary liquidation and parent liquidation decision
evidence_summary: ASLAN's sole operating subsidiary filed for voluntary liquidation on July 17, terminated all subsidiary employees and appointed provisional liquidators; the parent board also resolved it could not continue because of liabilities and would seek Cayman liquidation. July 18 was a vendor date proxy.
adjudication_note: Reject the July 18 bankruptcy metadata row and preserve the July 17 realized liquidation event separately.

evidence_item: operating subsidiary filing, employee terminations and parent liquidation resolution
evidence_summary: ASLAN SG filed for voluntary liquidation, appointed provisional liquidators and terminated all employees; the listed parent separately resolved that liabilities prevented continued business and that it would apply for Cayman liquidation.
adjudication_note: A++ ceiling: operating cessation and liquidation are realized, but the filing does not establish the terminal recovery or cancellation outcome for parent ADS holders.

evidence_item: 1-for-80 reverse split effective June 6
evidence_summary: Advaxis implemented a 1-for-80 reverse split effective and trading-adjusted on June 6, 2022 to support a Nasdaq uplisting application and increase authorized-but-unissued share availability for possible future financing.
adjudication_note: B only. The split and financing capacity are real, but no same-event issuance or old-equity destruction was established.

evidence_item: 1-for-80 split with completed Nasdaq unit offering
evidence_summary: American Rebel's 1-for-80 split became effective for Nasdaq trading on February 7 as part of a firm-commitment offering of 2,530,121 units at $4.15, each containing one common share and one immediately exercisable warrant at $5.1875.
adjudication_note: A: the new common and warrants were part of the same completed uplisting transaction, making this materially different from a stand-alone mechanical split.

evidence_item: implemented 1-for-75 reverse split and actual OTCQB trading date
evidence_summary: Spruce implemented a 1-for-75 reverse split for minimum-bid remediation and later reported that split-adjusted OTCQB trading began on August 7, 2025; older financing passages were not contemporaneous with this split.
adjudication_note: B only. Use the later filing's realized August 7 trading date rather than the earlier release's expected August 5 date, and do not backfill 2023 financing into the event.

evidence_item: 1-for-75 reverse split effective for February 9 trading
evidence_summary: Profusa announced that every 75 outstanding common shares would be consolidated into one and that PFSA would open on a post-split basis on February 9, 2026 to address Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance.
adjudication_note: B only. The reviewed evidence establishes a proportional compliance split, not contemporaneous dilution or terminal equity harm.

evidence_item: 1-for-75 share consolidation effective November 22 and trading November 25
evidence_summary: Psyence's 1-for-75 consolidation became effective November 22 and began post-consolidation trading on November 25, 2024; the November 26 vendor date was late.
adjudication_note: Reject November 26 and preserve the November 25 realized split-adjusted trading event separately.

evidence_item: 1-for-75 share consolidation for Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance
evidence_summary: Every 75 Psyence common shares became one, with the common shares beginning post-consolidation trading under PBM on November 25 as a Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance measure.
adjudication_note: B only. The consolidation was proportional and the filing did not establish a same-event issuance or old-equity destruction.

evidence_item: SPAC extension and trust amendment approvals
evidence_summary: Aura FAT shareholders approved charter and trust amendments extending the SPAC combination deadline and 2,728,914 public shares were redeemed for cash; the filing did not report bankruptcy or an insolvency liquidation.
adjudication_note: A funded public-share redemption and deadline extension are SPAC lifecycle mechanics, not judicial insolvency or unprotected common-equity death.

evidence_item: Item 1.03 Chapter 7 filing and cessation of operations
evidence_summary: Shapeways filed Chapter 7 and ceased all operations on July 2, 2024 under the Nasdaq ticker SHPW; SHPWQ and July 16 were later OTC identity and market-date proxies.
adjudication_note: Reject the SHPWQ July 16 metadata row and preserve the July 2 SHPW Chapter 7 filing separately.

evidence_summary: Shapeways and every subsidiary ceased operations and filed Chapter 7; all officers, employees and directors departed, debt accelerated and a trustee took responsibility for liquidating the estate.
adjudication_note: A++ ceiling: company and operations are terminal, but this filing does not itself establish the final cancellation or zero-recovery treatment of old common stock.

evidence_item: Item 1.03 Chapter 11 filing
evidence_summary: Ideanomics filed Chapter 11 on December 4, 2024 and pursued a sale of substantially all assets; the IDEXQ July 10 metadata row preceded the petition by almost five months and used a later OTC Q alias.
adjudication_note: Reject July 10 rather than leaking the December petition backward; preserve the petition and later plan-effective equity death on their own dates.

evidence_item: Item 1.03 Chapter 11 and Section 363 asset-sale process
evidence_summary: Ideanomics and debtor subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on December 4, remained debtors in possession and entered a stalking-horse process to sell all or substantially all assets.
adjudication_note: A++ at petition. Final old-common treatment was not yet legally effective and is recorded only in the later independent S event.

evidence_item: liquidation plan effective; all non-intercompany interests canceled with no distribution
evidence_summary: The Ideanomics liquidation plan became effective February 13, 2026; all debtor interests other than intercompany interests were automatically canceled, released and extinguished, and no holder of an interest received any plan distribution.
adjudication_note: S is dated only to plan effectiveness. FINRA's primary market notice confirms both final cancellation and no distribution; it is not backfilled to the December 2024 petition.

evidence_item: petition and later conversion chronology
evidence_summary: Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment filed Chapter 11 on June 28 under CSSE and the cases converted to Chapter 7 on July 10; CSSEQ on July 2 was neither legal milestone and was a later OTC identity proxy.
adjudication_note: Reject July 2 and separately preserve the June 28 petition and July 10 Chapter 7 conversion.

evidence_item: Chapter 11 petition chronology
evidence_summary: Chicken Soup for the Soul Entertainment and debtor subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on June 28, 2024 after debt-service failure, falling revenue, insufficient cash flow and liquidity challenges.
adjudication_note: A++ at petition; do not merge the later Chapter 7 conversion or infer final old-common treatment.

evidence_item: conversion of Chapter 11 cases to Chapter 7
evidence_summary: The Bankruptcy Court records that the CSSE cases converted from Chapter 11 to Chapter 7 on July 10, 2024, a separate realized liquidation escalation.
adjudication_note: A++ rather than S because conversion proves liquidation posture but not final cancellation or explicit zero recovery for old common.

evidence_item: voluntary NYSE delisting and OTCQX transition plan
evidence_summary: GAMCO's NYSE ticker was GBL through the October 6 delisting; GAMI was the subsequent OTCQX symbol. The candidate date was usable, but its ticker identity represented the post-event venue.
adjudication_note: Reject GAMI as the event-time ticker and preserve the October 6 GBL voluntary listing exit separately.

evidence_item: Form 25 effective date and OTCQX continuity plan
evidence_summary: GAMCO voluntarily ended GBL trading on NYSE when Form 25 took effect around October 6 to reduce reporting and compliance costs, while seeking continued liquidity on OTCQX under a new symbol.
adjudication_note: B only: national-exchange and SEC-reporting access narrowed, but the issuer sought OTCQX continuity and disclosed no forced or insolvency cause.

evidence_item: appointment of UK joint administrators
evidence_summary: Selina entered administration on July 22 under the Nasdaq ticker SLNA; joint administrators assumed control because the board saw no reasonable prospect of avoiding insolvency. SLNAF and July 26 were later OTC and delisting-consequence proxies.
adjudication_note: Reject the July 26 SLNAF bankruptcy metadata row; preserve the July 22 SLNA appointment of administrators separately.

evidence_item: UK Insolvency Act administration and control transfer
evidence_summary: Selina's board concluded insolvency could no longer reasonably be avoided, appointed joint administrators with no funding for subsidiaries, and transferred management of the parent's affairs, business and property from the board to those administrators.
adjudication_note: A++: parent control and solvency are terminal, but operating subsidiaries remained outside administration and final ordinary-share recovery was not established.

evidence_item: SPAC trust redemption, dissolution and requested delisting
evidence_summary: SEP Acquisition planned to redeem every public share for approximately $10.35474496 from its funded trust, then dissolve after failing to complete a combination; this was SPAC lifecycle mechanics, not bankruptcy.
adjudication_note: A funded trust redemption returning approximately $10.35 per public share is not judicial insolvency or uncompensated common-equity death.

evidence_item: SPAC trust redemption after combination deadline
evidence_summary: 10X Capital Venture Acquisition Corp III would redeem all public Class A shares for approximately $11.13 per share after failing to complete a business combination, cancel the July 12 meeting and wind up; this was a funded SPAC lifecycle event rather than bankruptcy.
adjudication_note: Reject bankruptcy. Public common was redeemed from trust for cash; warrant expiry is a separate instrument outcome and does not make the common-share event uncompensated equity death.

evidence_item: implemented 75-for-1 reverse split for Nasdaq compliance
evidence_summary: SMX automatically combined every 75 ordinary shares into one for Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance effective for July 15 trading. A separately described note-and-warrant issuance was later rescinded because the investor did not pay the proceeds.
adjudication_note: B only. The split was realized and proportional; the nearby financing cannot upgrade the event because the note and warrants were rescinded after non-payment of proceeds.

evidence_item: event-time INPX identity and one-for-75 reverse split
evidence_summary: Inpixon implemented the October 7 one-for-75 reverse split under ticker INPX for Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance. XTIA was a later issuer identity, and a later prospectus passage about a November 2020 financing did not describe the October 2022 split event.
adjudication_note: Reject XTIA as the event-time ticker and recover the proportional October 7 INPX split separately. Do not backfill either the embedded 2020 financing history or the separate October 2022 offering into the split date.

evidence_item: one-for-75 reverse split effective for October 7 trading
evidence_summary: Inpixon's one-for-75 reverse split became effective and began split-adjusted Nasdaq trading under INPX on October 7, 2022 to address minimum-bid compliance.
adjudication_note: B only. Preserve the exact INPX identity and October 7 effective/trading date; later offerings remain separate events.

evidence_item: filed one-for-75 reverse-split amendment with exact effective time
evidence_summary: Jaguar filed the Seventh Amendment with Delaware and its one-for-75 reverse split became effective at 12:01 a.m. on January 23, with split-adjusted Nasdaq trading that day; Nasdaq later confirmed minimum-bid compliance was regained.
adjudication_note: B only. The same-day filed charter amendment and exact legal effective time establish realization; future-tense wording alone does not make this merely an expected event.

evidence_form: SEC Form 8-K exhibit containing Nasdaq Hearings Panel decision
evidence_item: price-dislocation proxy resolved into four dated corporate events
evidence_summary: ADTX's June 9 twenty-one-day return was a market outcome spanning a repeated reverse split, severe equity deficiency, distressed secured-note refinancing, management departures and a pending Nasdaq appeal. The Panel's later decision established a separate June 25 suspension date; the price row itself is not event truth.
adjudication_note: Reject the return endpoint as a hard event label. Preserve the May 18 split, May 27 equity deficiency, June 3 secured refinancing and June 25 listing suspension separately.

evidence_item: filed one-for-27 reverse split effective for May 18 trading
evidence_summary: Aditxt filed a Delaware amendment for a one-for-27 reverse split effective May 15 and split-adjusted Nasdaq trading May 18, reducing approximately 13.77 million shares to about 510,123 while leaving authorized shares unchanged.
adjudication_note: B only. Repetition and unchanged authorized share headroom matter for review, but the split remained proportional and no same-event common issuance was established.

evidence_item: negative $35.17 million stockholders' equity and second Nasdaq delisting basis
evidence_summary: Nasdaq identified stockholders' equity of negative $35,174,386, failure of the $2.5 million equity standard and failure of both alternative standards, adding a second delisting basis to the existing minimum-bid determination.
adjudication_note: A: the negative equity and listing consequence were explicit and current, but the appeal stayed suspension and no court insolvency or old-common terminal outcome existed on May 27.

evidence_item: 35-percent-OID secured note refinancing collateralized by the only revenue-generating subsidiary
evidence_summary: Aditxt and Ignite rolled March and April notes into a new jointly owed senior secured series, added about $725,000 of cash, priced the notes at approximately $650 per $1,000 principal, pledged substantially all Ignite assets and equity, and set November 30 maturity.
adjudication_note: A: the cash need, discount, short maturity and core collateral are realized distress facts. No default on the new notes, court process, common conversion or terminal equity treatment was established, so A++ and S are prohibited.

evidence_form: SEC Form 8-K exhibit containing Nasdaq Hearings Panel decision
evidence_item: appeal denied and Nasdaq trading suspension effective June 25
evidence_summary: The Nasdaq Hearings Panel denied continued listing after seven reverse splits, persistent bid-price failure, negative equity and a non-compelling compliance plan; ADTX trading was ordered suspended at the June 25 open.
adjudication_note: A: the national-market access loss was final at the Panel level and date-specific, but it did not itself establish company death, old-common cancellation or zero recovery.

evidence_item: event-time EXN identity and continued TSX listing
evidence_summary: Excellon announced the January 30 NYSE American exit under ticker EXN, with continued TSX trading under EXN and an application for later U.S. OTC quotation; EXNRF was the post-delisting U.S. OTC identity.
adjudication_note: Reject EXNRF as the event-time ticker and preserve the January 30 EXN voluntary NYSE American exit separately.

evidence_item: voluntary NYSE American delisting with TSX continuity and La Negra acquisition condition
evidence_summary: Excellon expected January 30 to be the last NYSE American trading day under EXN because U.S. listing and reporting burdens outweighed their benefits and the exit was a condition of the pending La Negra mine acquisition; the shares remained listed on TSX and the issuer sought OTC quotation.
adjudication_note: B only: U.S. national-exchange and SEC-reporting access narrowed, but the same common equity continued on TSX, OTC quotation was sought and no forced or insolvency cause was disclosed.

evidence_form: issuer release distributed by Business Wire
evidence_item: event-time CIXX identity and continued TSX listing
evidence_summary: CI Financial announced the January 19 NYSE exit under CIXX while its common shares continued on TSX under CIX; CIXXF is a later U.S. OTC-style identity and was not the event-time NYSE ticker.
adjudication_note: Reject CIXXF as the event-time ticker and preserve the January 19 CIXX voluntary NYSE exit separately.

evidence_form: issuer release distributed by Business Wire
evidence_item: voluntary NYSE delisting with TSX continuity and U.S.-business IPO strategy
evidence_summary: CI Financial expected January 19 to be the last NYSE trading day under CIXX. Its board concluded that dual-listing and SEC-reporting costs outweighed the benefits as it pursued a separate U.S.-business IPO, while the same common equity continued on TSX under CIX.
adjudication_note: B only: U.S. market access narrowed and no replacement U.S. quotation was arranged, but the equity continued on TSX and the disclosed cause was strategic and cost-based rather than forced distress.

evidence_item: event-time EVK identity and later OTC Pink transition
evidence_summary: Ever-Glory identified EVK as the Nasdaq ticker through the December 23 last trading day and stated that OTC Pink trading would start December 27; EVKG was therefore a post-event OTC identity.
adjudication_note: Reject EVKG as the event-time ticker and preserve the December 23 EVK Nasdaq exit separately.

evidence_form: issuer release, SEC Form 25 and Form 15
evidence_item: voluntary Nasdaq exit after operating deterioration and unresolved listing deficiencies
evidence_summary: Ever-Glory ended Nasdaq trading under EVK on December 23 after three years of COVID-related sales harm, a fall below one dollar and unresolved minimum-bid noncompliance. The shares moved to OTC Pink on December 27 and the company later reported only 59 holders of record on Form 15.
adjudication_note: A: the issuer explicitly connected the exit to operating harm, sub-dollar pricing and unresolved listing noncompliance. OTC continuity prevents an A++ or S equity-death label.

evidence_item: Nasdaq ADS exit with Copenhagen ordinary-share continuity
evidence_summary: Zealand consolidated trading on Nasdaq Copenhagen, where its ordinary shares remained listed, because U.S. ADSs represented less than 1.5% of share capital and the company wanted to reduce costs and prioritize R&D.
adjudication_note: B only: the U.S. ADS venue closed, but the underlying ordinary shares retained their primary and more liquid Copenhagen listing and no forced or insolvency cause existed.

evidence_item: event-time BRCN Nasdaq identity before TSX consolidation
evidence_summary: Burcon's last Nasdaq session belonged to BRCN; BRCNF was the later U.S. OTC identity. The issuer consolidated trading on TSX after concluding that it was unlikely to cure the one-dollar bid-price deficiency and that Nasdaq costs outweighed limited secondary-market volume.
adjudication_note: Reject BRCNF as the event-time Nasdaq ticker and preserve the September 9 BRCN last-trading event separately.

evidence_item: voluntary Nasdaq exit after unresolved bid-price deficiency with TSX continuity
evidence_summary: Burcon ended Nasdaq trading under BRCN after determining that it was unlikely to regain the one-dollar minimum bid by September 28 and that a share consolidation was not beneficial. Its common shares continued on TSX, the primary venue.
adjudication_note: B: the unresolved bid-price issue is real, but the same common shares continued on TSX and no operating collapse, insolvency or old-common impairment was established.

evidence_item: event-time PTR NYSE ADS identity with HKSE and SSE continuity
evidence_summary: PetroChina's September 8 last NYSE session belonged to ADS ticker PTR; PTRCY was the subsequent OTC ticker. The underlying H and A shares continued on HKSE and SSE.
adjudication_note: Reject PTRCY as the event-time ticker and preserve the September 8 PTR ADS listing exit separately.

evidence_item: voluntary NYSE ADS delisting with HKSE and SSE underlying-share continuity
evidence_summary: PetroChina ended NYSE ADS trading under PTR because ADSs represented only 0.45% of total capital, trading was limited, regulatory administration was burdensome and NYSE had not been used for follow-on financing; HKSE and SSE listings remained available and ADS holders could obtain H shares.
adjudication_note: B only: this was a venue and depositary-program contraction with liquid home-market alternatives, not deterioration of the underlying company or common equity.

evidence_item: event-time SNP NYSE ADS identity with Hong Kong and Shanghai continuity
evidence_summary: China Petroleum & Chemical's September 8 U.S. last-trading event belonged to NYSE ADS ticker SNP; SNPTY was the later OTC identity. The underlying shares remained listed in Hong Kong and Shanghai.
adjudication_note: Reject SNPTY as the event-time ticker and preserve the September 8 SNP ADS listing exit separately.

evidence_item: voluntary NYSE ADS delisting with Hong Kong and Shanghai underlying-share continuity
evidence_summary: China Petroleum & Chemical ended NYSE ADS trading under SNP after citing the small ADS share base, limited ADS volume and long-term U.S. reporting burden. Its ordinary shares continued in Hong Kong and Shanghai.
adjudication_note: B only: the U.S. ADS venue ended for cost and volume reasons while the underlying equity retained its home-market listings.

evidence_item: event-time SHI NYSE ADS identity with HKEX and SSE continuity
evidence_summary: Sinopec Shanghai Petrochemical's September 2 last NYSE session belonged to ADS ticker SHI; SHIIY was a later OTC identity. The underlying H and A shares retained Hong Kong and Shanghai listings.
adjudication_note: Reject SHIIY as the event-time ticker and preserve the September 2 SHI ADS last-trading event separately.

evidence_item: voluntary NYSE ADS delisting with HKEX and SSE underlying-share continuity
evidence_summary: Sinopec Shanghai Petrochemical ended NYSE ADS trading under SHI after citing the small ADS share base, limited trading volume and U.S. administrative cost. The underlying Class H and A shares continued in Hong Kong and Shanghai.
adjudication_note: B only: an ADS and reporting-cost decision with home-market continuity is not forced delisting, insolvency or old-common impairment.

evidence_form: issuer announcement later reproduced in SEC annual report
evidence_item: event-time LFC NYSE ADS identity before LFCHY OTC trading
evidence_summary: China Life's September 1 last NYSE session belonged to ADS ticker LFC; LFCHY was the later OTC identity. The ADSs represented underlying H shares that continued on HKEX.
adjudication_note: Reject LFCHY as the event-time ticker and preserve the September 1 LFC ADS last-trading event separately.

evidence_form: issuer announcement later reproduced in SEC annual report
evidence_item: voluntary NYSE ADS delisting with HKEX underlying-share continuity
evidence_summary: China Life ended NYSE ADS trading under LFC after citing limited ADS volume and considerable U.S. listing and reporting cost. ADS holders retained a conversion route to underlying H shares listed on HKEX.
adjudication_note: B only: U.S. ADS liquidity ended, but the underlying H shares remained listed and deliverable; no company or common-equity death occurred.

evidence_item: Nasdaq exit with same-ticker OTCQX continuity
evidence_summary: United Bancshares expected August 26 to be the last Nasdaq trading day and arranged OTCQX quotation under the same UBOH ticker from August 29, citing the cost savings available to a bank holding company with fewer than 1,200 holders of record.
adjudication_note: B only: exchange and SEC-reporting access narrowed, but same-security OTCQX continuity and ongoing audited/regulatory financial reporting were explicit.

evidence_item: event-time ENIA NYSE ADS identity with Chilean-market continuity
evidence_summary: Enel Americas' final U.S. trading session belonged to NYSE ADS ticker ENIA; ENIAY was the later U.S. OTC identity. Ordinary shares remained listed on the Santiago and Chile Electronic exchanges.
adjudication_note: Reject ENIAY as the event-time ticker and preserve the June 17 ENIA last U.S. trading session separately.

evidence_item: voluntary NYSE ADS delisting with Chilean ordinary-share continuity
evidence_summary: Enel Americas ended U.S. ADS trading under ENIA after Enel S.p.A. ownership reached 82.3%, ADSs fell to about 2.49% of total shares and NYSE costs exceeded benefits. Ordinary shares continued on two Chilean exchanges and ADS holders could receive the underlying shares.
adjudication_note: B only: ownership concentration and cost rationalization reduced the U.S. venue, but the underlying ordinary shares and company remained publicly traded in Chile.

evidence_item: vendor bankruptcy-liquidation date replaced by wind-down, acceleration and later suspension dates
evidence_summary: eFFECTOR terminated all employees and entered a wind-down on June 24, received an insolvency-related loan default and immediate acceleration notice on June 25, and faced Nasdaq suspension on July 3. No Chapter 7, Chapter 11, receivership or other court petition was disclosed for July 2.
adjudication_note: Reject the July 2 bankruptcy label. Preserve the June 24 operating wind-down, June 25 debt acceleration and July 3 exchange suspension on their own official dates; none establishes final old-common cancellation.

evidence_item: all employees terminated, legacy board and officers departed, distressed wind-down specialist appointed
evidence_summary: eFFECTOR terminated all employees and planned to wind down operations. Seven directors and the CEO, CFO and CMO departed; a sole director and officer specializing in distressed-business wind-downs was appointed under a three-year engagement to develop the wind-down plan.
adjudication_note: A++: all-employee termination, governance replacement and a company-wide wind-down are severe terminal-company facts. S remains prohibited because no final legal instrument cancelled old common or fixed its distribution at zero.

evidence_item: material-adverse-change and insolvency defaults with all secured obligations immediately due
evidence_summary: Oxford Finance declared defaults under the material-adverse-change and insolvency clauses, made every loan obligation immediately due and payable, imposed the default interest rate and reserved all contractual remedies. The latest quarter had reported $19.4 million of outstanding principal.
adjudication_note: A: the default and acceleration are realized and severe, but they are lender remedies rather than a court insolvency filing, and the filing did not resolve collateral proceeds, unsecured recoveries or old-common treatment.

evidence_item: no-appeal Nasdaq suspension effective July 3 after public-shell and governance findings
evidence_summary: Nasdaq treated eFFECTOR as a public shell after the all-employee wind-down, identified board, committee and market-value deficiencies and scheduled suspension at the July 3 open. The company stated that it would not appeal and would file Form 15.
adjudication_note: A: national-market access ended and no appeal remained, but suspension is a consequence of the wind-down chain rather than proof of a bankruptcy petition or common-equity cancellation.

evidence_item: one-for-80 consolidation immediately after completed unit offering and full zero-price warrant exercise
evidence_summary: Elong closed an approximately $7 million offering of 21.7 million shares and 24.955 million warrants on February 27. By March 9 every warrant had been exercised through the zero-price option, producing 77,764,364 additional shares; the one-for-80 consolidation then began trading on March 12 with authorized shares reduced proportionally.
adjudication_note: A: the offering, warrant exercise and consolidation are realized and tightly aligned. The split alone would be B; no terminal old-common outcome supports A++ or S.

evidence_item: one-for-80 reverse split effective February 13 and trading February 14 under VRM
evidence_summary: Vroom's board selected a one-for-80 ratio after stockholder approval. The amendment became effective at 5:00 p.m. on February 13 and split-adjusted Nasdaq trading began February 14 under VRM; reviewed filings did not establish a completed contemporaneous financing.
adjudication_note: B only. Preserve the realized February 14 trading date and do not infer dilution from proportional split mechanics.

evidence_item: one-for-80 reverse split effective January 2 and trading January 3 with authorized shares unchanged
evidence_summary: Tenax's one-for-80 split became legally effective at 5:00 p.m. on January 2, 2024 and post-split trading began January 3. Authorized common shares were not reduced, increasing future issuance capacity, but no completed same-event financing was established.
adjudication_note: B only. Unreduced authorized shares create capacity, not proof that an issuance occurred.

evidence_item: later FFAI identity substituted for event-time FFIE reverse split
evidence_summary: Faraday Future's August 25 filing identifies FFIE, not the later FFAI symbol. The one-for-80 split became effective August 25 and began split-adjusted trading August 28; the filing separately disclosed a 15 million share sale on August 24.
adjudication_note: Reject FFAI as the 2023 event-time ticker. Preserve the FFIE split and preceding FFIE equity sale as separate official events.

evidence_item: event-time FFIE one-for-80 reverse split and proportional authorized-share reduction
evidence_summary: FFIE's one-for-80 split became effective at 5:00 p.m. on August 25 and split-adjusted Nasdaq trading began August 28. Authorized common shares were reduced from 1.765 billion to 154,437,500 and outstanding derivative terms were adjusted proportionally.
adjudication_note: B only for the split itself. The August 24 standby-equity sale is represented separately rather than being hidden inside split mechanics.

evidence_item: 15 million pre-split common shares sold under standby equity purchase agreement
evidence_summary: On August 24, before the reverse split took effect, FFIE sold 15 million Class A common shares to YA II PN at 97% of the three-day average VWAP under its standby equity purchase agreement.
adjudication_note: A: the share sale was completed and quantified. It is distinct from the proportional reverse split and does not prove terminal old-common loss.

evidence_item: later NEUE identity substituted for event-time BHG reverse split
evidence_summary: Bright Health Group's filing identifies BHG as the event-time NYSE symbol. The split became effective May 19 and BHG began one-for-80 split-adjusted trading on May 22; NEUE is a later issuer identity.
adjudication_note: Reject NEUE as the May 2023 ticker and preserve the BHG split on its realized trading date.

evidence_item: event-time BHG one-for-80 reverse split effective for May 22 trading
evidence_summary: Bright Health Group's one-for-80 split became effective at 5:00 p.m. on May 19 and split-adjusted NYSE trading began May 22 under the unchanged BHG symbol. Fractional interests were paid in cash.
adjudication_note: B only. A later financing agreement is not backfilled into the May 22 split event.

evidence_item: one-for-80 reverse split with completed Nasdaq unit and warrant offering
evidence_summary: ZIVO's one-for-80 split became effective and its common and warrants began Nasdaq trading on May 28. The linked underwritten offering of 2.76 million units at $5, each containing one share and one $5.50 warrant, closed June 2 for approximately $13.8 million gross proceeds; 414,000 additional warrants were exercised under the over-allotment option.
adjudication_note: A: completed common-and-warrant financing and Nasdaq trading were part of the same recapitalization chain. The split alone would be B.

evidence_item: one-for-75 OTC reverse split with authorized shares unchanged
evidence_summary: Infinite Group's one-for-75 split became effective October 19, with temporary IMCID trading before reversion to IMCI. Authorized shares were unchanged; the reviewed financing filing was dated November 30, forty-two days later, and is not treated as contemporaneous.
adjudication_note: B only. Authorized capacity is not a completed issuance, and the later note-and-warrant financing remains a separate event.

evidence_item: one-for-72 reverse split with simultaneous authorized-share increase
evidence_summary: AEON approved a one-for-72 split effective February 26 and separately increased authorized common shares from 500 million to 1.04 billion effective February 25. Outstanding shares fell from about 79.9 million to 1.1 million, creating very large post-split headroom, but the filing does not establish a completed same-event issuance.
adjudication_note: B only. The authorization creates severe issuance capacity but is not itself completed financing; keep later warrant exercises and offerings separately dated.

evidence_item: later DLAPQ identity and filing-date proxy for June 30 DLA Chapter 11 petitions
evidence_summary: Delta Apparel and its domestic subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on June 30, 2024 while the SEC cover identified NYSE American ticker DLA. July 1 was the filing and suspension date; DLAPQ was a later OTC identity.
adjudication_note: Reject DLAPQ and July 1 as the petition identity and date. Preserve the June 30 DLA Chapter 11 filing separately; an expected complete or significant loss is not final old-common cancellation.

evidence_item: parent and domestic subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 and pursued court-supervised asset sales
evidence_summary: DLA and its domestic subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions on June 30 in Delaware, continued as debtors in possession, sought DIP financing and launched structured asset sales including a roughly $28.03 million Salt Life stalking-horse transaction. The issuer expected common holders to suffer a complete or significant loss.
adjudication_note: A++: a realized parent-level court filing, debt acceleration and asset-sale process. S is prohibited until a final effective instrument cancels old common without distribution.

evidence_item: later DMTKQ identity and June 26 proxy for June 18 DMTK Chapter 11 petitions
evidence_summary: DermTech and DermTech Operations filed Chapter 11 on June 18, 2024 while the SEC cover identified Nasdaq ticker DMTK. The company intended to sell substantially all assets; DMTKQ and June 26 were later market identity and timing proxies.
adjudication_note: Reject the Q-suffix and June 26 proxy. Recover the June 18 DMTK petition; likely complete equity loss is not a final legal cancellation finding.

evidence_item: parent and operating subsidiary filed Chapter 11 to sell substantially all assets
evidence_summary: DMTK and DermTech Operations filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in Delaware on June 18, remained debtors in possession and announced an intended sale of substantially all assets. A 20% workforce reduction had already been completed and the issuer warned equity holders would likely experience a complete loss.
adjudication_note: A++: the petitions and substantially-all-asset sale intent are realized. S remains unavailable because likely loss language does not establish final cancellation or zero distribution.

evidence_item: later AUVIQ identity and May 28 proxy for May 24 AUVI Chapter 11 petitions
evidence_summary: Applied UV and SteriLumen filed Chapter 11 on May 24, 2024 while the SEC cover identified Nasdaq common ticker AUVI. AUVIQ and May 28 were later market identity and timing proxies.
adjudication_note: Reject AUVIQ and May 28 as the petition identity and date. Preserve the May 24 AUVI filing separately.

evidence_item: parent and wholly owned subsidiary filed Chapter 11 with near-zero operating cash
evidence_summary: AUVI and wholly owned SteriLumen filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in New York on May 24 and continued as debtors in possession. They reported only about $10,000 and $55,000 of cash respectively to fund post-petition operations and could not assure any distribution to common or preferred holders.
adjudication_note: A++: the court filings and near-zero cash are realized. Uncertainty about shareholder distributions is not the final no-distribution proof required for S.

evidence_item: May 22 pre-petition ISUNQ proxy for June 3 ISUN Chapter 11 filing
evidence_summary: iSun filed Chapter 11 on June 3, 2024 under ticker ISUN. The vendor's May 22 date preceded both the May 23 Nasdaq suspension and the June 3 petition, and the issuer explicitly said OTC Pink trading began under ISUN, not ISUNQ.
adjudication_note: Reject the May 22 bankruptcy label and ISUNQ identity. Preserve the June 3 ISUN petition; Nasdaq suspension and Form 25 remain separate market-access events.

evidence_item: parent and subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 with debt acceleration and continued DIP operations
evidence_summary: ISUN and eleven subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in Delaware on June 3 under case 24-11144, continued as debtors in possession and triggered immediate maturity under multiple debt instruments. The issuer warned holders could experience significant or complete loss.
adjudication_note: A++: the parent-level petitions and debt acceleration are realized. Possible significant or complete loss is not a final effective cancellation and no-distribution instrument.

evidence_item: pre-petition April 17 OSAPQ proxy for May 7 OSAP Chapter 11 filing
evidence_summary: ProSomnus filed Chapter 11 on May 7, 2024 after its common began OTC trading under OSAP on April 18. The vendor's April 17 OSAPQ row predates both the OTC transition and the petition and does not preserve event-time identity.
adjudication_note: Reject April 17 and OSAPQ. Preserve the May 7 OSAP petition; the proposed no-recovery treatment was not yet an effective plan and cannot support S at filing.

evidence_form: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.03 and restructuring support agreement
evidence_item: pre-negotiated Chapter 11 with DIP funding, debt acceleration and proposed no-recovery old equity treatment
evidence_summary: OSAP and debtor subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on May 7 with a restructuring support agreement, up to $13 million of DIP financing, $41.67 million principal acceleration and at least $9 million of proposed new-money equity. The proposed plan allocated new common to subordinated secured noteholders and proposed no recovery for other equity interests.
adjudication_note: A++: the petition, DIP structure and debt acceleration are realized. The no-recovery term remains proposed until plan confirmation and effectiveness, so S is prohibited at this date.

evidence_item: later ACORQ identity and April 11 proxy for April 1 ACOR Chapter 11 petitions
evidence_summary: Acorda and subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on April 1, 2024 while the SEC cover identified Nasdaq ticker ACOR. The April 11 ACORQ row is a later OTC market identity and date proxy.
adjudication_note: Reject ACORQ and April 11 as petition truth. Preserve the April 1 ACOR Chapter 11 filing and its court-supervised sale process separately.

evidence_item: parent and subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 with $185 million stalking-horse asset sale and DIP financing
evidence_summary: ACOR and certain subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on April 1 in New York, continued as debtors in possession and pursued a court-supervised sale of substantially all assets to Merz for $185 million subject to higher bids. The restructuring included a proposed $60 million DIP facility and automatic acceleration of the 2024 convertible notes.
adjudication_note: A++: the petition, DIP structure and substantially-all-asset sale process are realized. The filing does not by itself establish final old-common cancellation and no distribution.

evidence_item: February 3 TWNPQ proxy for January 26 TWNP Chapter 11 petition
evidence_summary: Twin Hospitality and its direct and indirect subsidiaries, together with parent FAT Brands and the other debtors, filed Chapter 11 on January 26, 2026 while Twin's Nasdaq Class A common ticker was TWNP. The February 3 TWNPQ row is a later market-identity and date proxy.
adjudication_note: Reject TWNPQ and February 3 as petition truth. Preserve the January 26 TWNP petition, the February 4 Nasdaq suspension and later OTC events on their own dates.

evidence_item: public subsidiary and related debtors commenced Chapter 11 under joint FAT Brands cases
evidence_summary: TWNP, its direct and indirect subsidiaries, parent FAT Brands and the other debtors commenced voluntary Chapter 11 cases in the Southern District of Texas on January 26 under case 26-90126 and continued as debtors in possession. The issuer warned common holders could suffer complete or significant loss but did not report final cancellation or zero distribution.
adjudication_note: A++: the petition and debtor-in-possession status are realized. Expected complete or significant loss is not the final effective old-common cancellation and no-distribution evidence required for S.

evidence_item: February 3 TWNPQ delisting proxy one day before TWNP Nasdaq suspension
evidence_summary: Nasdaq scheduled suspension of TWNP Class A common stock for the opening of business on February 4, 2026 because of the Chapter 11 cases and residual-equity concerns. The February 3 TWNPQ row is neither the event-time Nasdaq ticker nor the effective suspension date.
adjudication_note: Reject February 3 and TWNPQ as the delisting event. Preserve the February 4 TWNP suspension as an A-grade consequence linked to the January 26 Chapter 11 event.

evidence_item: bankruptcy-driven Nasdaq trading suspension with expected Pink Limited transition
evidence_summary: Nasdaq determined to delist TWNP under Rules 5101, 5110(b) and IM-5101-1 after the Chapter 11 filing and residual-equity concerns, suspended trading at the February 4 open and expected the common to move to Pink Limited. The company did not appeal.
adjudication_note: A: national-market access ended on a precise date, but the suspension is a consequence of the Chapter 11 chain and does not independently prove old-common cancellation or zero recovery.

evidence_item: substantially all Twin Peaks assets sold through approximately $359.5 million credit bid
evidence_summary: On June 15 the TWNP debtors closed the sale of substantially all Twin Peaks restaurant, bar, franchise and brand assets for an approximately $359.5 million credit bid comprising DIP and prepetition securitization obligations, plus assumed liabilities. The filing does not establish a confirmed effective plan or old-common distribution.
adjudication_note: A++: the substantially-all-asset credit-bid sale actually closed. Without a final effective plan stating old-common cancellation and distribution, the event remains below S.

evidence_item: February 3 FATAQ proxy for January 26 FAT Chapter 11 petition
evidence_summary: FAT Brands and its direct and indirect subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on January 26, 2026 while its Nasdaq securities were FAT Class A, FATBB Class B and FATBP preferred. The February 3 FATAQ row is a later market-identity and date proxy for the Class A security.
adjudication_note: Reject FATAQ and February 3 as petition truth. Preserve the January 26 FAT petition, February 4 multi-security Nasdaq suspension and later OTC events on their own dates.

evidence_item: parent and all direct and indirect subsidiaries commenced Chapter 11 and continued as debtors in possession
evidence_summary: FAT Brands and each direct and indirect subsidiary commenced voluntary Chapter 11 cases in the Southern District of Texas on January 26 under case 26-90126 and continued as debtors in possession. The filing identified FAT, FATBB and FATBP as the event-time Nasdaq securities and warned of possible complete or significant loss without final equity treatment.
adjudication_note: A++: the petitions, debtor-in-possession operations and debt acceleration are realized. Possible complete or significant loss is not the final effective old-common treatment required for S.

evidence_item: February 3 FATAQ delisting proxy one day before FAT Nasdaq suspension
evidence_summary: Nasdaq scheduled suspension of FAT Class A, FATBB Class B and FATBP preferred securities for the opening of business on February 4 because of the Chapter 11 cases and residual-equity concerns. The February 3 FATAQ row is a later Class A identity and pre-effective-date proxy.
adjudication_note: Reject February 3 and FATAQ as the delisting event. Preserve the February 4 FAT/FATBB/FATBP suspension as an A-grade consequence linked to the January 26 Chapter 11 event.

evidence_item: bankruptcy-driven Nasdaq suspension of three listed security classes with expected Pink Limited transition
evidence_summary: Nasdaq determined to delist FAT, FATBB and FATBP under Rules 5101, 5110(b) and IM-5101-1 after the Chapter 11 filing and residual-equity concerns, suspended trading at the February 4 open and expected the securities to move to Pink Limited. The company did not appeal.
adjudication_note: A: national-market access ended for three securities on a precise date, but the suspension is a consequence of Chapter 11 and does not independently establish cancellation or zero recovery.

evidence_item: substantially all FAT Brands assets sold through approximately $595 million credit bid
evidence_summary: On June 15 the FAT Brands debtors closed the sale of substantially all restaurant, bar, entertainment, franchise and brand assets for an approximately $595 million credit bid comprising DIP and prepetition note obligations, plus assumed liabilities. The filing does not establish a confirmed effective plan or old-common distribution.
adjudication_note: A++: the substantially-all-asset credit-bid sale actually closed. Without a final effective plan stating old-common cancellation and distribution, the event remains below S.

evidence_item: FELPQ volume-crash and post-event ticker proxy for same-day FELPU Chapter 11 petition
evidence_summary: Foresight Energy and all subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on March 10, 2020, but the issuer identified the event-time OTCQX unit ticker as FELPU. Sharadar's identity history records the later FELPU-to-FELPQ change on April 6, so the March 10 FELPQ price row is a post-event identity and market-outcome proxy rather than the legal event itself.
adjudication_note: Reject the price observation as a hard event and reject FELPQ as the March 10 identity. Preserve the FELPU petition, later plan confirmation and FELPQ plan-effective terminal outcome on their own dates.

evidence_form: SEC Form 8-K Items 1.01, 1.03 and 2.04 plus Exhibit 99.2
evidence_item: parent, general partner and all subsidiaries filed pre-arranged Chapter 11 with DIP and debt equitization
evidence_summary: FELPU, its general partner and all subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the Eastern District of Missouri on March 10 under case 20-41308-659. The RSA had support from lenders holding more than 73% of approximately $1.4 billion of first- and second-lien claims, contemplated substantially all funded debt being equitized, and included a committed $100 million new-money DIP facility and proposed $225 million exit facility.
adjudication_note: A++ on the petition date: court filing, broad debtor scope and debt equitization are realized, but the old-unit terminal treatment had not yet become effective.

evidence_form: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.03 and court confirmation order
evidence_item: court confirmed plan providing no recovery to common and subordinated units
evidence_summary: The Bankruptcy Court confirmed Foresight's plan on June 24. The confirmed plan reduced more than $1 billion of debt, eliminated about $94 million of anticipated annual cash interest and provided no recovery to 80,996,773 common units or 64,954,691 subordinated units, but the issuer expressly said the effective date remained subject to conditions.
adjudication_note: A++ only on June 24: court confirmation and zero-recovery treatment are strong, but the issuer stated that effectiveness remained conditional. S is reserved for the June 30 effective date.

evidence_item: plan effective; all common and subordinated units extinguished without consideration and no recovery
evidence_summary: Foresight's confirmed plan became effective on June 30 after all conditions were satisfied or waived. Holders received no recovery, all existing common and subordinated units were extinguished without consideration, the partnership and related dissolving entities were slated for dissolution, and operating assets moved to creditor-owned successor entities.
adjudication_note: S is anchored only to June 30 plan effectiveness. Explicit zero recovery plus extinguishment without consideration satisfies finality and is not backfilled to the March petition or June 24 confirmation.

evidence_form: SEC Forms 6-K dated May 21, May 22 and July 3, 2024
evidence_item: CZOOF bankruptcy-liquidation row conflates subsidiary administration, NYSE suspension and later parent winding up
evidence_summary: On May 21 three English operating and holding subsidiaries entered administration while the Cayman parent, whose NYSE ticker was still CZOO, only decided to seek shareholder approval for a winding up. NYSE suspended CZOO that day, CZOOF began as the post-suspension OTC identity, and the parent did not enter voluntary winding up until shareholders approved it on July 2.
adjudication_note: Reject CZOOF, May 21 and bankruptcy liquidation as one parent-level event. Preserve the subsidiary administrations, NYSE suspension, final delisting and parent voluntary winding up as separate events on their exact dates. The Teneo exhibit's generic bankruptcy-and-insolvency service description is not event evidence.

evidence_item: three material English subsidiaries entered administration and administrators assumed control
evidence_summary: Cazoo Holdings Limited, Cazoo Ltd and Cazoo Properties Limited entered UK administration on May 21 and joint administrators from Teneo were appointed to manage their affairs, business and property. The listed Cayman parent was not itself in administration and only resolved to seek a winding up.
adjudication_note: A++ for the realized administration of the three material English subsidiaries. Do not describe the Cayman parent as bankrupt or in liquidation on this date, and do not use the later CZOOF ticker.

evidence_item: NYSE immediately suspended CZOO after material-subsidiary administrations and announced delisting proceedings
evidence_summary: NYSE notified Cazoo on May 21 that it would commence proceedings to delist the Class A ordinary shares and suspended trading immediately under Section 802.01D after the subsidiary administrations and parent winding-up disclosure. The issuer did not intend to appeal and expected OTC Pink trading.
adjudication_note: Use CZOO for the security suspended from NYSE on May 21. CZOOF is the post-suspension OTC alias, not the event-time NYSE identity.

evidence_item: Class A ordinary shares were finally delisted from NYSE effective June 3
evidence_summary: The issuer's winding-up proxy states that its Class A ordinary shares were delisted by NYSE effective June 3, 2024 and were then trading on the OTC Pink Marketplace.
adjudication_note: Preserve June 3 as the final NYSE delisting date, separate from the May 21 immediate suspension and OTC ticker transition.

evidence_item: shareholders commenced insolvent Cayman voluntary winding up, appointed liquidators and closed share transfer books
evidence_summary: On July 2 shareholders approved voluntary winding up because Cazoo Group Ltd was unable to pay its debts, joint voluntary liquidators were appointed immediately, all directors resigned, share transfer books closed, all realizable assets had been disposed of and the company expected no remaining proceeds for shareholders.
adjudication_note: A++ only. Winding up commenced and transfers stopped, but the filing says the process will continue until affairs are finally wound up and liquidators later seek dissolution. Expected zero proceeds is not explicit final cancellation or completed dissolution, so S is prohibited.
